- macOS: Add an option macos_show_window_title_in_menubar to not show the current window title in the menu-bar (#1066)
- macOS: Workaround for cocoa bug that could cause the mouse cursor to become hidden in other applications in rare circumstances (#1218)
- macOS: Allow assigning only the left or right Option key to work as the
Alt key. See macos_option_as_alt for details (#1022)
- Fix using remote control to set cursor text color causing errors when creating new windows (#1326)
- Fix window title for minimized windows not being updated (#1332)
- macOS: Fix using multi-key sequences to input text ignoring the first few key presses if the sequence is aborted (#1311)
- macOS: Add a number of common macOS keyboard shortcuts
- macOS: Reduce energy consumption by not rendering occluded windows
- Fix scrollback pager history not being cleared when clearing the main scrollback buffer (#1387)
- macOS: When closing a top-level window only switch focus to the previous kitty window if it is on the same workspace (#1379)
- macOS: Fix sync_to_monitor not working on Mojave.
- macOS: Use the system cursor blink interval by default
cursor_blink_interval.
- Wayland: Use the kitty Wayland backend by default. Can be switched back
to using XWayland by setting the environment variable:
KITTY_DISABLE_WAYLAND=1
- Add a no-append setting to clipboard_control to disable
the kitty copy concatenation protocol extension for OSC 52.
- Update to using the Unicode 12 standard
- Unicode input kitten: Allow using the arrow keys in code mode to go to next and previous unicode symbol.
- macOS: Fix specifying initial window size in cells not working correctly on Retina screens (#1444)
- Fix a regression in version 0.13.0 that caused background colors of space characters after private use unicode characters to not be respected (#1455)
- Only update the selected text to clipboard when the selection is finished, not continuously as it is updated. (#1460)
- Allow setting active_border_color to none to not draw a border
around the active window (#805)
- Use negative values for mouse_hide_wait to hide the mouse cursor
immediately when pressing a key (#1534)
- When encountering errors in kitty.conf report them to the user
instead of failing to start.
- Allow the user to control the resize debounce time via
resize_debounce_time.
- Remote control: Make the kitten @ set-font-size command more capable. It can now increment font size and reset it. It also only acts on the active top-level window, by default (#1581)
- When launching child processes set the PWD environment variable
(#1595)
- X11: use the window manager’s native full-screen implementation when making windows full-screen (#1605)
- Mouse selection: When extending by word, fix extending selection to non-word characters not working well (#1616)
0.13.3 [2019-01-19]¶
- icat kitten: Add a --stdin option to control if image data is read from
STDIN (#1308)
- hints kitten: Start hints numbering at one instead of zero by default. Added
an option --hints-offset to control it. (#1289)
- Fix a regression in the previous release that broke using background for cursor_text_color (#1288)
- macOS: Fix dragging kitty window tabs in traditional full screen mode causing crashes (#1296)
- macOS: Ensure that when running from a bundle, the bundle kitty exe is preferred over any kitty in PATH (#1280)
- macOS: Fix a regression that broke mapping of ctrl+tab (#1304)
- Add a list of user-created kittens to the docs
- Fix a regression that broke changing mouse wheel scroll direction with
negative wheel_scroll_multiplier values in full-screen applications
like vim (#1299)
- Fix background_opacity not working with pure white backgrounds
(#1285)
- macOS: Fix “New OS Window” dock action not working when kitty is not focused (#1312)
- macOS: Add aliases for close window and new tab actions that conform to common Apple shortcuts for these actions (#1313)
- macOS: Fix some kittens causing 100% CPU usage
0.13.2 [2019-01-04]¶
- Add a new option tab_title_template to control how tab titles
are formatted. In particular the template can be used to display
the tab number next to the title (#1223)
- Report the current foreground processes as well as the original child process, when using kitty @ ls
- Use the current working directory of the foreground process for the *_with_cwd actions that open a new window with the current working directory.
- Add a new copy_or_interrupt action that can be mapped to kbd:ctrl+c. It
will copy if there is a selection and interrupt otherwise (#1286)
- Fix setting background_opacity causing window margins/padding to be slightly
different shade from background (#1221)
- Handle keyboards with a “+” key (#1224)
- Fix Private use Unicode area characters followed by spaces at the end of text not being rendered correctly (#1210)
- macOS: Add an entry to the dock menu to open a new OS window (#1242)
- macOS: Fix scrolling very slowly with wheel mice not working (#1238)
- Fix changing cursor_text_color via remote control not working
(#1229)
- Add an action to resize windows that can be mapped to shortcuts in kitty.conf (#1245)
- Fix using the new_tab !neighbor action changing the order of the
non-neighboring tabs (#1256)
- macOS: Fix momentum scrolling continuing when changing the active window/tab (#1267)
0.13.1 [2018-12-06]¶
- Fix passing input via the pipe action to a program without a window not working.
- Linux: Fix a regression in the previous release that caused automatic selection of bold/italic fonts when using aliases such as “monospace” to not work (#1209)
- Fix resizing window smaller and then restoring causing some wrapped lines to not be properly unwrapped (#1206)
0.13.0 [2018-12-05]¶
- Add an option scrollback_pager_history_size to tell kitty to store
extended scrollback to use when viewing the scrollback buffer in a pager
(#970)
- Modify the kittens sub-system to allow creating custom kittens without any
user interface. This is useful for creating more complex actions that can
be bound to key presses in kitty.conf. See
doc:kittens/custom. (#870)
- Add a new nth_window action that can be used to go to the nth window and
also previously active windows, using negative numbers. Similarly, goto_tab now accepts negative numbers to go to previously active tabs
(#1040)
- Allow hiding the tab bar completely, by setting tab_bar_style to hidden. (#1014)
- Allow private use unicode characters to stretch over more than a single neighboring space (#1036)
- Add a new touch_scroll_multiplier option to modify the amount
scrolled by high precision scrolling devices such as touchpads (#1129)
- icat kitten: Implement reading image data from STDIN, if STDIN is not connected to a terminal (#1130)
- hints kitten: Insert trailing spaces after matches when using the
--multiple option. Also add a separate --add-trailing-space option to control this behavior (#1132)
- Fix the *_with_cwd actions using the cwd of the overlay window rather
than the underlying window’s cwd (#1045)
- Fix incorrect key repeat rate on wayland (#1055)
- macOS: Fix drag and drop of files not working on Mojave (#1058)
- macOS: Fix IME input for East Asian languages (#910)
- macOS: Fix rendering frames-per-second very low when processing large amounts of input in small chunks (#1082)
- macOS: Fix incorrect text sizes calculated when using an external display that is set to mirror the main display (#1056)
- macOS: Use the system default double click interval (#1090)
- macOS: Fix touch scrolling sensitivity low on retina screens (#1112)
- Linux: Fix incorrect rendering of some fonts when hinting is disabled at small sizes (#1173)
- Linux: Fix match rules used as aliases in Fontconfig configuration not being respected (#1085)
- Linux: Fix a crash when using the GNU Unifont as a fallback font (#1087)
- Wayland: Fix copying from hidden kitty windows hanging (#1051)
- Wayland: Add support for the primary selection protocol implemented by some compositors (#1095)
- Fix expansion of env vars not working in the env directive
(#1075)
- Fix mouse_hide_wait only taking effect after an event such as cursor
blink or key press (#1073)
- Fix the set_background_opacity action not working correctly
(#1147)
- Fix second cell of emoji created using variation selectors not having the same attributes as the first cell (#1109)
- Fix focusing neighboring windows in the grid layout with less than 4 windows not working (#1115)
- Fix ctrl+shift+special key not working in normal and application keyboard modes (#1114)
- Add a terminfo entry for full keyboard mode.
- Fix incorrect text-antialiasing when using very low background opacity (#1005)
- When double or triple clicking ignore clicks if they are “far” from each other (#1093)
- Follow xterm’s behavior for the menu key (#597)
- Fix hover detection of URLs not working when hovering over the first colon and slash characters in short URLs (#1201)
0.12.3 [2018-09-29]¶
0.12.2 [2018-09-24]¶
- A new last_used_layout function that can be mapped to a shortcut to
switch to the previously used window layout (#870)
- New neighboring_window and move_window functions to switch to
neighboring windows in the current layout, and move them around, similar to
window movement in vim (#916)
- A new pipe function that can be used to pipe the contents of the screen
and scrollback buffer to any desired program running in a new window, tab or
overlay window. (#933)
- Add a new kitty --start-as command line flag to start kitty
full-screen/maximized/minimized. This replaces the --start-in-fullscreen flag introduced in the previous release (#935)
- When mapping the new_tab action allow specifying that the tab should open
next to the current tab instead of at the end of the tabs list (#979)
- macOS: Add a new macos_thicken_font to make text rendering
on macs thicker, which makes it similar to the result of
sub-pixel antialiasing (#950)
- macOS: Add an option macos_traditional_fullscreen to make
full-screening of kitty windows much faster, but less pretty. (#911)
- Fix a bug causing incorrect line ordering when viewing the scrollback buffer if the scrollback buffer is full (#960)
- Fix drag-scrolling not working when the mouse leaves the window confines (#917)
- Workaround for broken editors like nano that cannot handle newlines in pasted text (#994)
- Linux: Ensure that the python embedded in the kitty binary build uses UTF-8 mode to process command-line arguments (#924)
- Linux: Handle fonts that contain monochrome bitmaps (such as the Terminus TTF font) (#934)
- Have the kitty --title flag apply to all windows created
using kitty --session (#921)
- Revert change for backspacing of wide characters in the previous release, as it breaks backspacing in some wide character aware programs (#875)
- Fix kitty @set-colors not working for tab backgrounds when using the fade tabbar style (#937)
- macOS: Fix resizing semi-transparent windows causing the windows to be invisible during the resize (#941)
- Linux: Fix window icon not set on X11 for the first OS window (#961)
- macOS: Add an macos_custom_beam_cursor option to use a special
mouse cursor image that can be seen on both light and dark backgrounds
(#359)
- Remote control: Fix the focus_window command not focusing the
top-level OS window of the specified kitty window (#1003)
- Fix using focus_follows_mouse causing text selection with the
mouse to malfunction when using multiple kitty windows (#1002)
0.12.1 [2018-09-08]¶
- Add a new --start-in-fullscreen command line flag to start
kitty in full screen mode (#856)
- macOS: Fix a character that cannot be rendered in any font causing font fallback for all subsequent characters that cannot be rendered in the main font to fail (#799)
- Linux: Do not enable IME input via ibus unless the GLFW_IM_MODULE=ibus environment variable is set. IME causes key processing latency and even
missed keystrokes for many people, so it is now off by default.
- Fix backspacing of wide characters in wide-character unaware programs not working (#875)
- Linux: Fix number pad arrow keys not working when Numlock is off (#857)
- Wayland: Implement support for clipboard copy/paste (#855)
- Allow mapping shortcuts using the raw key code from the OS (#848)
- Allow mapping of individual key-presses without modifiers as shortcuts
- Fix legacy invocation of icat as kitty icat not working (#850)
- Improve rendering of wavy underline at small font sizes (#853)
- Fix a regression in 0.12.0 that broke dynamic resizing of layouts (#860)
- Wayland: Allow using the kitty --class command line flag
to set the app id (#862)
- Add completion of the kitty command for the fish shell (#829)
- Linux: Fix XCompose rules with no defined symbol not working (#880)
- Linux: Fix crash with some Nvidia drivers when creating tabs in the first top level-window after creating a second top-level window. (#873)
- macOS: Diff kitten: Fix syntax highlighting not working because of a bug in the 0.12.0 macOS package
0.12.0 [2018-09-01]¶
- Preserve the mouse selection even when the contents of the screen are scrolled or overwritten provided the new text does not intersect the selected lines.
- Linux: Implement support for Input Method Extensions (multilingual input using standard keyboards) via IBus (#469)
- Implement completion for the kitty command in bash and zsh. See Shell integration.
- Render the text under the cursor in a fixed color, configurable via
the option cursor_text_color (#126)
- Add an option env to set environment variables in child processes
from kitty.conf
- Add an action to the clear_terminal function to scroll the screen
contents into the scrollback buffer (#1113)
- Implement high precision scrolling with the trackpad on platforms such as macOS and Wayland that implement it. (#819)
- macOS: Allow scrolling window contents using mouse wheel/trackpad even when the window is not the active window (#729)
- Remote control: Allow changing the current window layout with a new kitten @ goto-layout command (#845)
- Remote control: Allow matching windows by the environment variables of their child process as well
- Allow running kittens via the remote control system (#738)
- Allow enabling remote control in only some kitty windows
- Add a keyboard shortcut to reset the terminal (ctrl+shift+delete). It
takes parameters so you can define your own shortcuts to clear the
screen/scrollback also (#747)
- Fix one-pixel line appearing at window edges at some window sizes when displaying images with background opacity enabled (#741)
- diff kitten: Fix error when right hand side file is binary and left hand side file is text (#752)
- kitty @ new-window: Add a new option kitten @ new-window --window-type to create top-level OS windows (#770)
- macOS: The focus_follows_mouse option now also works across top-level kitty OS windows
(#754)
- Fix detection of URLs in HTML source code (URLs inside quotes) (#785)
- Implement support for emoji skin tone modifiers (#787)
- Round-trip the zwj unicode character. Rendering of sequences containing zwj is still not implemented, since it can cause the collapse of an unbounded number of characters into a single cell. However, kitty at least preserves the zwj by storing it as a combining character.
- macOS: Disable the custom mouse cursor. Using a custom cursor fails on dual GPU machines. I give up, Apple users will just have to live with the limitations of their choice of OS. (#794)
- macOS: Fix control+tab key combination not working (#801)
- Linux: Fix slow startup on some systems caused by GLFW searching for joysticks. Since kitty does not use joysticks, disable joystick support. (#830)
0.11.3 [2018-07-10]¶
- Draw only the minimum borders needed for inactive windows. That is only the borders
that separate the inactive window from a neighbor. Note that setting
a non-zero window margin overrides this and causes all borders to be drawn.
The old behavior of drawing all borders can be restored via the
draw_minimal_borders setting in kitty.conf. (#699)
- macOS: Add an option macos_window_resizable to control if kitty
top-level windows are resizable using the mouse or not (#698)
- macOS: Use a custom mouse cursor that shows up well on both light and dark backgrounds (#359)
- macOS: Workaround for switching from fullscreen to windowed mode with the titlebar hidden causing window resizing to not work. (#711)
- Fix triple-click to select line not working when the entire line is filled (#703)
- When dragging to select with the mouse “grab” the mouse so that if it strays into neighboring windows, the selection is still updated (#624)
- When clicking in the margin/border area of a window, map the click to the nearest cell in the window. Avoids selection with the mouse failing when starting the selection just outside the window.
- When drag-scrolling stop the scroll when the mouse button is released.
- Fix a regression in the previous release that caused pasting large amounts of text to be duplicated (#709)
0.11.2 [2018-07-01]¶
- Linux: Allow using XKB key names to bind shortcuts to keys not supported by GLFW (#665)
- kitty shell: Ignore failure to read readline history file. Happens if the user migrates their kitty cache directory between systems with incompatible readline implementations.
- macOS: Fix an error in remote control when using --listen-on (#679)
- hints kitten: Add a kitty +kitten hints --multiple option to select
multiple items (#687)
- Fix pasting large amounts of text very slow (#682)
- Add an option single_window_margin_width to allow different margins
when only a single window is visible in the layout (#688)
- Add a kitty --hold command line option to stay open after the child process exits (#667)
- diff kitten: When triggering a search scroll to the first match automatically
- kitty --debug-font-fallback also prints out what basic fonts were matched
- When closing a kitty window reset the mouse cursor to its default shape and ensure it is visible (#655).
- Remote control: Speed-up reading of command responses
- Linux installer: Fix installer failing on systems with python < 3.5
- Support “-T” as an alias for “--title” (#659)
- Fix a regression in the previous release that broke using
--debug-config with custom key mappings (#695)
0.11.1 [2018-06-17]¶
- diff kitten: Implement searching for text in the diff (#574)
- Add an option startup_session to kitty.conf to specify a
default startup session (#641)
- Add a command line option kitty --wait-for-single-instance-window-close to make kitty --single-instance wait for the closing of the newly opened
window before quitting (#630)
- diff kitten: Allow theming the selection background/foreground as well
- diff kitten: Display CRLF line endings using the unicode return symbol instead of <d> as it is less intrusive (#638)
- diff kitten: Fix default foreground/background colors not being restored when kitten quits (#637)
- Fix kitten @ set-colors --all not working when more than one window
present (#632)
- Fix a regression that broke the legacy increase/decrease_font_size actions
- Clear scrollback on reset (#631)
0.11.0 [2018-06-12]¶
- A new tab bar style “fade” in which each tab’s edges fade into the background.
See tab_bar_style and tab_fade for details. The old look can be
restored by setting tab_bar_style to separator.
- Pre-compiled binaries with all bundled dependencies for Linux (#595)
- A new kitten to create dock panels on X11 desktops showing the output from arbitrary terminal programs.
- Reduce data sent to the GPU per render by 30% (commit: 8dea5b3e3)
- Implement changing the font size for individual top level (OS) windows (#408)
- When viewing the scrollback in less using ctrl+shift+h and kitty
is currently scrolled, position the scrollback in less to match kitty’s
scroll position. (#148)
- ssh kitten: Support all SSH options. It can now be aliased directly to ssh for convenience. (#591)
- icat kitten: Add kitty +kitten icat --print-window-size to easily
detect the window size in pixels from scripting languages (#581)
- hints kitten: Allow selecting hashes from the terminal with
ctrl+shift+p>h useful for git commits. (#604)
- Allow specifying initial window size in number of cells in addition to pixels (#436)
- Add a setting to control the margins to the left and right of the tab-bar (#584)
- When closing a tab switch to the last active tab instead of the right-most tab (#585)
- Wayland: Fix kitty not starting when using wl_roots based compositors (#157)
- Wayland: Fix mouse wheel/touchpad scrolling in opposite direction to other apps (#594)
- macOS: Fix the new OS window keyboard shortcut (ctrl+shift+n) not
working if no kitty window currently has focus. (#524)
- macOS: Keep kitty running even when the last window is closed. This is in
line with how applications are supposed to behave on macOS (#543).
There is a new option (macos_quit_when_last_window_closed) to control
this.
- macOS: Add macOS standard shortcuts for copy, paste and new OS window (⌘+C, ⌘+V, ⌘+N)
- Add a config option (editor) to set the EDITOR kitty uses (#580)
- Add a config option (x11_hide_window_decorations) to hide window
decorations under X11/Wayland (#607)
- Add an option to @set-window-title to make the title change non-permanent (#592)
- Add support for the CSI t escape code to query window and cell sizes (#581)
- Linux: When using layouts that map the keys to non-ascii characters, map shortcuts using the ascii equivalents, from the default layout. (#606)
- Linux: Fix fonts not being correctly read from TrueType Collection (.ttc) files (#577)
- Fix inactive_text_alpha also applying to the tab bar (#612)
- hints kitten: Fix a regression that caused some blank lines to be not be displayed.
- Linux: Include a man page and the HTML docs when building the linux-package
- Remote control: Fix kitty @ sometimes failing to read the response from kitty. (#614)
- Fix kitty @ set-colors not working with the window border colors. (#623)
- Fix a regression in 0.10 that caused incorrect rendering of the status bar in irssi when used inside screen. (#621)
0.10.1 [2018-05-24]¶
- Add a kitten to easily ssh into servers that automatically copies the
terminfo files over. kitty +kitten ssh myserver.
- diff kitten: Make the keyboard shortcuts configurable (#563)
- Allow controlling background_opacity via either keyboard shortcuts or remote control. Note that you must set dynamic_background_opacity yes in kitty.conf first. (#569)
- diff kitten: Add keybindings to scroll by page
- diff kitten: Fix incorrect syntax highlighting for a few file formats such as yaml
- macOS: Fix regression that caused the macos_option_as_alt setting to always be disabled for all OS windows in a kitty instance after the first window (#571)
- Fix Ctrl+Alt+Space not working in normal and application keyboard modes (#562)
0.10.0 [2018-05-21]¶
- A diff kitten to show side-by-side diffs with syntax highlighting and support for images. See diff kitten.
- Make windows in the various kitty layouts manually resizable. See Layouts for details.
- Implement support for the SGR faint escape code to make text blend into the background (#446).
- Make the hints kitten a little smarter (commit: ad1109b6f) so that URLs that stretch over multiple lines are detected. Also improve detection of surrounding brackets/quotes.
- Make the kitty window id available as the environment variable
KITTY_WINDOW_ID (#532).
- Add a “fat” layout that is similar to the “tall” layout but vertically oriented.
- Expand environment variables in config file include directives
- Allow programs running in kitty to read/write from the clipboard (commit: 889ca7791). By default only writing is allowed. This feature is supported in many terminals, search for OSC 52 clipboard to find out more about using it.
- Fix moving cursor outside a defined page area incorrectly causing the cursor to be placed inside the page area. Caused incorrect rendering in neovim, in some situations (#542).
- Render a couple more powerline symbols directly, bypassing the font (#550).
- Fix ctrl+alt+<special> not working in normal and application keyboard (#548).
- Partial fix for rendering Right-to-left languages like Arabic. Rendering of Arabic is never going to be perfect, but now it is at least readable.
- Fix Ctrl+backspace acting as plain backspace in normal and application keyboard modes (#538).
- Have the paste_from_selection action paste from the clipboard on platforms that do not have a primary selection such as Wayland and macOS (#529)
- Fix cursor_stop_blinking_after=0 not working (#530)
0.9.1 [2018-05-05]¶
- Show a bell symbol on the tab if a bell occurs in one of the windows in the tab and the window is not the currently focused window
- Change the window border color if a bell occurs in an unfocused window. Can be disabled by setting the bell_border_color to be the same as the inactive_border_color.
- macOS: Add support for dead keys
- Unicode input: When searching by name search for prefix matches as well as whole word matches
- Dynamically allocate the memory used for the scrollback history buffer. Reduces startup memory consumption when using very large scrollback buffer sizes.
- Add an option to not request window attention on bell.
- Remote control: Allow matching windows by number (visible position).
- macOS: Fix changing tab title and kitty shell not working
- When triple-clicking select all wrapped lines belonging to a single logical line.
- hints kitten: Detect bracketed URLs and don’t include the closing bracket in the URL.
- When calling pass_selection_to_program use the current directory of the child process as the cwd of the program.
- Add macos_hide_from_tasks option to hide kitty from the macOS task switcher
- macOS: When the macos_titlebar_color is set to background change the titlebar colors to match the current background color of the active kitty window
- Add a setting to clear all shortcuts defined up to that point in the config file(s)
- Add a setting (kitty_mod) to change the modifier used by all the default kitty shortcuts, globally
- Fix Shift+function key not working
- Support the F13 to F25 function keys
- Don’t fail to start if the user deletes the hintstyle key from their fontconfig configuration.
- When rendering a private use unicode codepoint and a space as a two cell ligature, set the foreground colors of the space cell to match the colors of the first cell. Works around applications like powerline that use different colors for the two cells.
- Fix passing @text to other programs such as when viewing the scrollback buffer not working correctly if kitty is itself scrolled up.
- Fix window focus gained/lost events not being reported to child programs when switching windows/tabs using the various keyboard shortcuts.
- Fix tab title not changing to reflect the window title when switching between different windows in a tab
- Ignore -e if it is specified on the command line. This is for compatibility with broken software that assumes terminals should run with an -e option to execute commands instead of just passing the commands as arguments.
0.9.0 [2018-04-15]¶
- A new kitty command shell to allow controlling kitty via commands. Press ctrl+shift+escape to run the shell.
- The hints kitten has become much more powerful. Now in addition to URLs you can use it to select word, paths, filenames, lines, etc. from the screen. These can be inserted into the terminal, copied to clipboard or sent to external programs.
- Linux: Switch to libxkbcommon for keyboard handling. It allows kitty to support XCompose and dead keys and also react to keyboard remapping/layout change without needing a restart.
- Add support for multiple-key-sequence shortcuts
- A new remote control command set-colors to change the current and/or configured colors.
- When double-clicking to select a word, select words that continue onto the next/prev line as well.
- Add an include directive for the config files to read multiple config files
- Improve mouse selection for windows with padding. Moving the mouse into the padding area now acts as if the mouse is over the nearest cell.
- Allow setting all 256 terminal colors in the config file
- Fix using kitty --single-instance to open a new window in a running kitty instance, not respecting the --directory flag
- URL hints: Exclude trailing punctuation from URLs
- URL hints: Launch the browser from the kitty parent process rather than the hints kitten. Fixes launching on some systems where xdg-open doesn’t like being run from a kitten.
- Allow using rectangle select mode by pressing shift in addition to the rectangle select modifiers even when the terminal program has grabbed the mouse.
0.8.4 [2018-03-31]¶
- Fix presence of XDG_CONFIG_DIRS and absence of XDG_CONFIG_HOME preventing kitty from starting
- Revert change in last release to cell width calculation. Instead just clip the right edges of characters that overflow the cell by at most two pixels
0.8.3 [2018-03-29]¶
- Fix a regression that broke the visual bell and invert screen colors escape code
- Allow double-click and triple-click + drag to extend selections word at a time or line at a time
- Add a keyboard shortcut to set the tab title
- Fix setting window title to empty via OSC escape code not working correctly
- Linux: Fix cell width calculation incorrect for some fonts (cell widths are now calculated by actually rendering bitmaps, which is slower but more accurate)
- Allow specifying a system wide kitty config file, for all users
- Add a --debug-config command line flag to output data about the system and kitty configuration.
- Wayland: Fix auto-repeat of keys not working
0.8.2 [2018-03-17]¶
- Allow extending existing selections by right clicking
- Add a configurable keyboard shortcut and remote command to set the font size to a specific value
- Add an option to have kitty close the window when the main processes running in it exits, even if there are still background processes writing to that terminal
- Add configurable keyboard shortcuts to switch to a specific layout
- Add a keyboard shortcut to edit the kitty config file easily
- macOS: Fix restoring of window size not correct on Retina screens
- macOS: Add a facility to specify command line arguments when running kitty from the GUI
- Add a focus-tab remote command
- Fix screen not being refreshed immediately after moving a window.
- Fix a crash when getting the contents of the scrollback buffer as text
0.8.1 [2018-03-09]¶
- Extend kitty’s remote control feature to work over both UNIX and TCP sockets, so now you can control kitty from across the internet, if you want to.
- Render private use unicode characters that are followed by a space as a two character ligature. This fixes rendering for applications that misuse private-use characters to display square symbols.
- Fix Unicode emoji presentation variant selector causing new a fallback font instance to be created
- Fix a rare error that prevented the Unicode input kitten from working sometimes
- Allow using Ctrl+Alt+letter in legacy keyboard modes by outputting them as Ctrl+letter and Alt+letter. This matches other terminals’ behavior.
- Fix cursor position off-by-one on horizontal axis when resizing the terminal
- Wayland: Fix auto-repeat of keys not working
- Wayland: Add support for window decorations provided by the Wayland shell
- macOS: Fix URL hints not working
- macOS: Fix shell not starting in login mode on some computers
- macOS: Output errors into console.app when running as a bundle
0.8.0 [2018-02-24]¶
- A framework for kittens, that is, small terminal programs designed to run inside kitty and extend its capabilities. Examples include unicode input and selecting URLs with the keyboard.
- Input arbitrary unicode characters by pressing Ctrl+Shift+u. You can choose characters by name, by hex code, by recently used, etc. There is even and editable Favorites list.
- Open URLs using only the keyboard. kitty has a new “hints mode”. Press Ctrl+Shift+e and all detected URLs on the screen are highlighted with a key to press to open them. The facility is customizable so you can change what is detected as a URL and which program is used to open it.
- Add an option to change the titlebar color of kitty windows on macOS
- Only consider Emoji characters with default Emoji presentation to be two cells wide. This matches the standard. Also add support for the Unicode Emoji variation presentation selector.
- Prevent video tearing during high speed scrolling by syncing draws
to the monitor’s refresh rate. There is a new configuration option to
control this sync_to_monitor.
- When displaying only a single window, use the default background color of the window (which can be changed via escape codes) as the color for the margin and padding of the window.
- Add some non standard terminfo capabilities used by neovim and tmux.
- Fix large drop in performance when using multiple top-level windows on macOS
- Fix save/restore of window sizes not working correctly.
- Remove option to use system wcwidth(). Now always use a wcwidth() based on the Unicode standard. Only sane way.
- Fix a regression that caused a few ligature glyphs to not render correctly in rare circumstances.
- Browsing the scrollback buffer now happens in an overlay window instead of a new window/tab.
0.7.1 [2018-01-31]¶
- Add an option to adjust the width of character cells
- Fix selecting text with the mouse in the scrollback buffer selecting text from the line above the actually selected line
- Fix some italic fonts having the right edge of characters cut-off, unnecessarily
0.7.0 [2018-01-24]¶
- Allow controlling kitty from the shell prompt/scripts. You can open/close/rename windows and tabs and even send input to specific windows. See the README for details.
- Add option to put tab bar at the top instead of the bottom
- Add option to override the default shell
- Add “Horizontal” and “Vertical” window layouts
- Sessions: Allow setting titles and working directories for individual windows
- Option to copy to clipboard on mouse select
- Fix incorrect reporting of mouse move events when using the SGR protocol
- Make alt+backspace delete the previous word
- Take the mouse wheel multiplier option in to account when generating fake key scroll events
- macOS: Fix closing top-level window does not transfer focus to other top-level windows.
- macOS: Fix alt+arrow keys not working when disabling the macos_option_as_alt config option.
- kitty icat: Workaround for bug in ImageMagick that would cause some images to fail to display at certain sizes.
- Fix rendering of text with ligature fonts that do not use dummy glyphs
- Fix a regression that caused copying of the selection to clipboard to only copy the visible part of the selection
- Fix incorrect handling of some unicode combining marks that are not re-ordered
- Fix handling on non-BMP combining characters
- Drop the dependency on libunistring
0.6.1 [2017-12-28]¶
- Add an option to fade the text in inactive windows
- Add new actions to open windows/tabs/etc. with the working directory set to the working directory of the current window.
- Automatically adjust cell size when DPI changes, for example when kitty is moved from one monitor to another with a different DPI
- Ensure underlines are rendered even for fonts with very poor metrics
- Fix some emoji glyphs not colored on Linux
- Internal wcwidth() implementation is now auto-generated from the unicode standard database
- Allow configuring the modifiers to use for rectangular selection with the mouse.
- Fix incorrect minimum wayland version in the build script
- Fix a crash when detecting a URL that ends at the end of the line
- Fix regression that broke drawing of hollow cursor when window loses focus
0.6.0 [2017-12-18]¶
- Support background transparency via the background_opacity option. Provided that your OS/window manager supports transparency, you can now have kitty render pixels that have only the default background color as semi-transparent.
- Support multiple top level (OS) windows. These windows all share the sprite texture cache on the GPU, further reducing overall resource usage. Use the shortcut ctrl+shift+n to open a new top-level window.
- Add support for a daemon mode using the --single-instance command line option. With this option you can have only a single kitty instance running. All future invocations simply open new top-level windows in the existing instance.
- Support colored emoji
- Use CoreText instead of FreeType to render text on macOS
- Support running on the “low power” GPU on dual GPU macOS machines
- Add a new “grid” window layout
- Drop the dependency on glfw (kitty now uses a modified, bundled copy of glfw)
- Add an option to control the audio bell volume on X11 systems
- Add a command line switch to set the name part of the WM_CLASS window property independently.
- Add a command line switch to set the window title.
- Add more options to customize the tab-bar’s appearance (font styles and separator)
- Allow drag and drop of files into kitty. On drop kitty will paste the file path to the running program.
- Add an option to control the underline style for URL highlighting on hover
- X11: Set the WINDOWID environment variable
- Fix middle and right buttons swapped when sending mouse events to child processes
- Allow selecting in a rectangle by holding down Ctrl+Alt while dragging with the mouse.
0.5.1 [2017-12-01]¶
- Add an option to control the thickness of lines in box drawing characters
- Increase max. allowed ligature length to nine characters
- Fix text not vertically centered when adjusting line height
- Fix unicode block characters not being rendered properly
- Fix shift+up/down not generating correct escape codes
- Image display: Fix displaying images taller than two screen heights not scrolling properly
0.5.0 [2017-11-19]¶
- Add support for ligature fonts such as Fira Code, Hasklig, etc. kitty now uses harfbuzz for text shaping which allow it to support advanced OpenType features such as contextual alternates/ligatures/combining glyphs/etc.
- Make it easy to select fonts by allowing listing of monospace fonts using: kitty list-fonts
- Add an option to have window focus follow mouse
- Add a keyboard shortcut (ctrl+shift+f11) to toggle fullscreen mode
- macOS: Fix handling of option key. It now behaves just like the alt key on Linux. There is an option to make it type unicode characters instead.
- Linux: Add support for startup notification on X11 desktops. kitty will now inform the window manager when its startup is complete.
- Fix shell prompt being duplicated when window is resized
- Fix crash when displaying more than 64 images in the same session
- Add support for colons in SGR color codes. These are generated by some applications such as neovim when they mistakenly identify kitty as a libvte based terminal.
- Fix mouse interaction not working in apps using obsolete mouse interaction protocols
- Linux: no longer require glew as a dependency
0.4.2 [2017-10-23]¶
- Fix a regression in 0.4.0 that broke custom key mappings
- Fix a regression in 0.4.0 that broke support for non-QWERTY keyboard layouts
- Avoid using threads to reap zombie child processes. Also prevent kitty from hanging if the open program hangs when clicking on a URL.
0.4.0 [2017-10-22]¶
- Support for drawing arbitrary raster graphics (images) in the terminal via a new graphics protocol. kitty can draw images with full 32-bit color using both ssh connections and files/shared memory (when available) for better performance. The drawing primitives support alpha blending and z-index. Images can be drawn both above and below text. See Terminal graphics protocol. for details.
- Refactor kitty’s internals to make it even faster and more efficient. The CPU
usage of kitty + X server while doing intensive tasks such as scrolling a
file continuously in less has been reduced by 50%. There are now two
configuration options repaint_delay and input_delay you can use to
fine tune kitty’s performance vs CPU usage profile. The CPU usage of kitty +
X when scrolling in less is now significantly better than most (all?) other
terminals. See Performance.
- Hovering over URLs with the mouse now underlines them to indicate they can be clicked. Hold down Ctrl+Shift while clicking to open the URL.
- Selection using the mouse is now more intelligent. It does not add blank cells (i.e. cells that have no content) after the end of text in a line to the selection.
- The block cursor in now fully opaque but renders the character under it in the background color, for enhanced visibility.
- Allow combining multiple independent actions into a single shortcut
- Add a new shortcut to pass the current selection to an external program
- Allow creating shortcuts to open new windows running arbitrary commands. You can also pass the current selection to the command as an arguments and the contents of the screen + scrollback buffer as stdin to the command.

articles.title: Midterm elections 2026: all the news
articles.body:
The 2026 midterm elections will determine the scope of President Donald Trump’s power in his final two years in office, and signal what voters care about going into the 2028 presidential election. While this year’s races are expected to be most broadly defined by affordability issues, there are several topics impacting the tech industry that appear to be on voters’ minds.
Among them are concerns about data centers, and whether voters will have to bear the burden of higher energy costs, AI safety, and the rapid expansion of surveillance technology through Flock. There’s also the question of how to tax billionaires’ wealth in California, a topic that has driven heavy tech spending and creative stock class structures meant to keep tech executives from fleeing the state should a ballot measure pass.
The next Congress is likely to continue grappling with how to regulate AI, and stem the data center backlash, among other issues. How that conversation shapes up, and which tech CEOs are hauled to testify on Capitol Hill, will be shaped by the outcome of November 3rd.
- Maine Republican Susan Collins concedes Senate seat in a tech-fueled race. The longtime senator counted tech executives like Palantir CEO Alex Karp and venture capitalists Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz among her donors. Democratic challenger Troy Jackson also received some billionaire support, but no obvious tech ties. Maine almost became the first state to pause data centers, before the governor vetoed the moratorium.
- Democrat projected to win Ohio seat that Republicans warned could spell trouble for data centers. NBC News projects Democrat Sherrod Brown will win back his former Senate seat from Republican Jon Husted, who Brown had labeled “the face of data centers.” The National Republican Senatorial Committee warned in a leaked August memo that if Husted loses “and data centers get the blame, politicians across the country will take notice — and they will not go near the next one.”
- Data center-dense Texas turns blue. Both Democrats James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa are projected by NBC News to win their Senate and gubernatorial races, respectively. Hinojosa has called for a moratorium on data center development in the state, while Talarico has favored ending tax incentives and creating an “AI dividend” for Americans to share in profits. Voters in Texas agree: They hate data centers Justine Calma
- Data center backlash wasn’t quite enough to flip Florida. The pro-data center Republican Byron Donalds has won the race for governor, according to the AP. He beat Democrat David Jolly with just over 50 percent of the vote — a far tighter margin than predecessor Ron DeSantis in 2022.
- Democrats leaned into Big Tech and AI opposition this cycle. Democratic candidates touted their credentials taking on the tech industry far more than in prior election cycles, an analysis by public policy group Reset Tech finds. Between 2020 and 2024, only two Democratic ads used the phrase “Big Tech.” From 2025 to 2026, that number was 154.
- Fulton County, GA may need to rescan 1,000 ballots tonight because of scanner malfunctions. A county election official asked the election board for approval to rescan ballots from two scanners experiencing equipment issues. One scanner seemed to wrongly display that it had a paper jam, CBS News reports, while another displayed an error after a voter accidentally rolled over its cable with a wheelchair.
- Things still seem to be going fairly smoothly. The nonpartisan Election Protection Coalition says it’s received over 8,000 hotline calls today, but the reported concerns are fairly standard for large elections. Rev. Dr. Katie Sexton Wood, executive director of the Arizona Faith Network, says there’s been no verified reports of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) near Arizona polling spots.
- Michigan officials contacted DOJ about reports of election monitors speaking with poll workers. State officials got reports that DOJ monitors asked poll workers in Dearborn for their training materials, Michigan Attorney General office spokesperson Danny Wimmer confirms. The DOJ’s team overseeing Michigan monitors told state officials such actions were not part of their training, Wimmer says, and that the team would follow up. But in a statement to The Verge, DOJ spokesperson Kiersten Pels says the questions monitors asked were “typical questions about election official training” that are standard on forms provided to monitors and the same as those asked under the previous administration. Pels added that the DOJ has not confimed that monitors have asked for training materials, but told Michigan officials they’d remind monitors they can ask about training, but “don’t need to request training materials.” Update: Added DOJ statement.
- This Election Day, remember which party ran against EVs and tethered us all to the gas pump It’s the midterms! Here’s a fun fact for you as you head to the polls: Gas prices today are the highest ever recorded for a US Election Day. The national average for a gallon of gasoline is $4.12 and $6.28 for a gallon of diesel, according to GasBuddy. Meanwhile, the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which is maintained by the US Department of Energy as a safeguard during energy crises, is down to 282.2 million barrels of crude, the lowest level in 44 years. Read Article >
- Severe weather is affecting some voters across the country. In Florida, more than 20 polling sites are being moved due to intense flooding. Storms in the Southwest have also impacted some polling locations in Colorado, Newsweek reports, while Utah will let some voters impacted by flooding return ballots electronically, and Arizona officials are warning voters to check travel updates.
- A ballot scanner issue is impacting a New York suburb. Polling sites across Westchester County are experiencing an issue with their voting machines, but officials say residents can still safely cast their ballots. Election officials have a backup protocol in place to ensure voting can continue. Voting Machine Snags Are Reported in New York Suburbs [New York Times]
- Election protection hotline has received 3,000 calls this morning. The nonpartisan coalition running the 866-OUR-VOTE hotline says the calls range from asking about general information, to reporting long lines, lack of signage, or voting equipment issues. Texas, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and New York account for the most calls. So far, no calls about federal agents at the polls.
- DOJ sends 1,000 election monitors to watch polls in every state. Federal election monitors are a standard procedure, but this year the Trump administration has expanded it to the “largest monitoring effort in history.” States have prepared to make sure they don’t interfere, as the administration has taken several steps this year to assert more oversight of state-run elections.
- Prop 45 in California could be hiding a loophole for data centers A high-stakes California ballot measure pitched as a fast track for “essential” infrastructure could wind up giving data center developers a loophole to evade public scrutiny, environmental advocates warn. Proposition 45 would shorten timelines for state-mandated environmental assessments for eligible projects and make it more difficult for residents to challenge those projects in court. Proponents say passing the measure would help alleviate the state’s housing shortage and meet rising electricity demand with new renewable energy projects. Environmental groups and some legal experts, however, warn that data center developers backing the proposition could escape scrutiny if Prop 45 becomes law. Read Article >
- Another election year, another tech company war room. OpenAI is the latest tech company (and according to Politico, the first major AI company) to set up a command center for fighting election misinfo and abuse of its systems, approaching the second major AI-era US election: The Election Operations Center will begin running this week until all votes are counted, to identify the potential spread of misinformation or other efforts to disrupt the elections. It’s meant in large part to combat abuse of the company’s own tools like ChatGPT, monitoring real-time events and fielding reports of unexpected behavior from models or cases of suspected violations of their platform’s terms.
- Voters in Texas agree: They hate data centers Ask Texas NAACP president Gary Bledsoe what it’s been like to see data center developers descend upon Austin and its surrounding suburbs and he can rattle off project after project facing opposition from locals. There’s the fight in Taylor over plans to build a data center at a site that’s supposed to be a park. Temple, around 40 miles away, is another sore spot, Bledsoe says. The mayor and City Council members there face recall attempts over data center developments. And some 30 miles outside of Austin, San Marcos became the first city in all of Texas to ban data centers. Read Article >
- Data center backlash is uniting America If there’s one issue that seems to activate all kinds of voters in 2026, it’s data centers. The rapid buildout of these massive server storage facilities — and the infrastructure construction and expenses that come with them — has sparked local opposition in communities across the country and become a major issue in many congressional and gubernatorial campaigns. At the same time, tech money has been pouring into many of these races. Leading the Future, a super PAC backed by venture capitalist Marc Andreessen and OpenAI President Greg Brockman, has already spent $45 million in a year. And Public First Action, an Anthropic-backed group that says it supports AI safeguards, says it’s raised $80 million. Both have funded Democratic and Republican-aligned groups. Other super PACs see an opportunity to push for stricter AI policies, like the recently created Tomorrow Together, which launched $4 million in ads for battleground House races, with messages about data center development and AI safety. Read Article >
- Republican politicians have embraced anti-Indian racism — and it’s costing them votes Two years ago, University of Houston student Vasant Bhatt was doing everything he could to help Republicans regain power. He knocked doors for Sen. Ted Cruz’s reelection campaign and helped organize his community for Donald Trump, two victories he, like many other Republicans, celebrated in 2024. But this week, Bhatt did something unexpected: He voted for Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico, and he publicly urged others to do the same. Bhatt, whose father is a small-business owner, tells The Verge he was initially drawn to the Republican Party due to its economic principles. “The strong belief in individual liberty and limited government,” he says, led him to identify as a conservative. More recently, however, another aspect of his family’s experience has driven him away from the party. As an Indian American, Bhatt feels increasingly unwelcome in a party where racist rhetoric is becoming far too common. Read Article >
- Meta made a deal to keep Mark Zuckerberg from leaving California over its billionaire tax. It said in a filing that Zuckerberg “was evaluating relocating his primary residence” if California’s Proposition 40 passes. As Bloomberg reports, Meta’s board issued special shares so that he wouldn’t have to leave: Zuckerberg gets non-voting shares he can sell for liquidity without reducing his voting control. In return, he has committed to remain in California — or wherever Meta is headquartered — for eight years while he remains in a full-time leadership role.
- Trump is giving Nick Shirley $10,000 and launching a $25 million fraud bounty program Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance said on Tuesday that the Trump administration was giving right-wing YouTuber Nick Shirley $10,000 and launching a $25 million bounty program for members of the public to report fraud. In December 2025, Shirley published a viral video alleging fraud at daycares in Minnesota that were operated by members of the local Somali community. Shirley lingered in parking lots and asked to enter childcare centers, taking refusals as evidence that the centers weren’t actually caring for children. The video quickly went viral, triggering a massive governmental response: Federal immigration agents descended on the Minneapolis area, and the Trump administration froze Minnesota’s federal funding for childcare. Shirley has since visited other states in the US under similar pretenses, showing up unannounced to grocery stores and hospice centers in search of evidence of fraud. Vance and others in the administration publicly praised Shirley, who has since become a mainstay in the MAGA-aligned content creator ecosystem. He’s helped popularize a genre of so-called independent journalism popular on the right in which content creators and influencers confront businesses or people they suspect of fraud or crime as the basis for their online content. Harassment — or even immigration crackdowns — often follow. Read Article >
- Democrats think cracking down on AI could give them an edge Democrats could win back control of Congress this November, and if they do, they’ll need to decide how to approach one of the country’s newest and thorniest political issues: AI. Polls predict Democrats will flip at least one chamber of Congress in the midterm elections, which would put committee leadership back in their hands. That could usher in a wave of newfound scrutiny for AI companies. Top Democrats on key committees have already signaled their willingness to press the industry on tax credits tied to data centers and recent hacking incidents, and would be able to set committee agendas if they take over, allowing them to call CEOs to testify in Congress and demand documents that explain companies’ inner workings. Read Article >
- Tech billionaires have reportedly donated over $340 million to fight a wealth tax in California. According to The Guardian, the campaign they’re funding is spending over $1 million per day trying to defeat Proposition 40, which would enact a one-time 5 percent tax on California’s billionaires. Google co-founder Sergey Brin is reportedly the biggest donor, contributing at least $102 million, alongside other tech executives: The donors to the no campaign are a who’s who of Silicon Valley, including the Palantir co-founder Peter Thiel, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, DoorDash CEO Tony Xu, Stripe CEO Patrick Collison, crypto magnate Chris Larsen and several prominent venture capitalists.
- Elon Musk has donated over $276 million to Republican midterm efforts Elon Musk has handed out at least $276 million to Republican groups since July, The New York Times reports, making him both the party’s top known donor and the biggest established midterm donor. $158 million of that money — one of the largest political donations in American history — has been funneled into the Senate Leadership Fund, the main super PAC that aims to secure and maintain a Republican Senate majority. Among others, it’s fighting to retain the party’s Senate seat in Texas, which serves as a major hub for Musk’s business empire. He’s also donated over $76 million to America PAC, a super PAC Musk founded in 2024 that canvasses for hard-to-reach Republican voters. Smaller amounts have also been given to other conservative groups, including: Read Article >
- The midterms are going to be a data security nightmare One messy database is threatening to disenfranchise thousands or even millions of registered voters, while leaving even more at risk of intimidation or data breaches, in the name of solving a problem that barely exists. As the 2026 midterm elections approach, election and privacy experts are sounding alarms about the Department of Homeland Security’s Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) Program, which President Donald Trump’s administration has expanded to ostensibly catch noncitizens voting. Experts say that amounts to a dangerous, error-prone effort to centralize voter data. “The federal government doesn’t have the authority to do any of that and doesn’t have the expertise either,” says Eileen O’Connor, senior counsel at the Brennan Center. “Inserting themselves into the day-to-day functioning of state elections is unprecedented and disturbing.” Read Article >
- Democrats preview how they’d go after the Ticketmaster settlement if they regain power A handful of Democrats called an unofficial hearing on Capitol Hill Monday to slam the Department of Justice’s “trivial” and “pathetic” settlement with Live Nation-Ticketmaster, previewing how they might go after Trump administration antitrust deals if they win back congressional power in November. While the DOJ settlement with Live Nation, which came one week into trial and with a promise of up to $280 million, received copious pushback, Democrats don’t at the moment have the power in either chamber to set committee agendas. That meant that Monday’s so-called shadow hearing looked different than most official proceedings. Instead of sitting at the elevated seats behind the dais, the lawmakers sat at tables below, eye level with witnesses including California Attorney General Rob Bonta, one of the AGs continuing the fight against Live Nation-Ticketmaster, ousted Trump administration antitrust official Roger Alford, and several entertainment industry players, including a member of the band The Hold Steady. Several artists asked to appear at the forum declined out of fear for their livelihoods, according to House Judiciary Committee Ranking Member Jamie Raskin (D-MD), who co-hosted the forum with Senate Homeland Security permanent subcommittee on investigations Ranking Member Richard Blumenthal (D-CT). Read Article >
More Stories

articles.title: Thoughts From a Tsunami
articles.body:
Thoughts From a Tsunami
Posted on November 4, 2026 Posted by John Scalzi 40 Comments
Thank you, America, you understood the assignment.
But also, Jesus, what a faceplant for Trump and all of the Republican party. Do you understand how much you have to have fucked up that Kansas elected a Democratic senator? That literally hasn’t happened since the New Deal. Do you know how much you have to have fucked up to have Mississippi still in play as of the writing of this post? MISSISSIPPI. You don’t get any more Republican territory than Mississippi, goddamn. Except maybe South Carolina, which just elected a Democrat to Lindsey Graham’s old seat. North Carolina elected a Democratic senator and flipped one of their state legislative bodies to Democrat.
And holy shit, Texas! Not just senator Talarico, not just Governor Hinojosa, but as far as I can tell every single statewide office went blue, down to and including the railroad commissioner. The Democrats look like they’re going to flip the Texas house, too. FUCKING TEXAS WENT BLUE Y’ALL. Not just a little, but a lot.
(And Ohio, too, where I live, but I’ll get to that in a second.)
Now, credit is due to the Democrats actually fielding decent candidates this year and doing the work — you don’t get Abdul El-Sayad into the senate (as an example) without Abdul El-Sayad being a generationally sensational candidate. But let’s make no mistake that this blue wave is a response to an administration and political party so corrupt and awful and, yes, actually fucking evil, that a certain number of people who have perennially voted red either voted blue or stayed at home, and a lot of blue-voting people who might have stayed home for a mid-term went out of their way to get to the polls this time around.
This election was a rebuke and a repudiation, and I hope to the sweet and merry God above that the Democrats remember that when they’re seated in January. They were not elected to office to play nice with the fascists in the halls of power. They were elected to punch them in the face, repeatedly, the president most of all, but, be assured, not only him. There is to be a lot of punching going on.
Now, Ohio. When I went to bed last night Amy Acton was elected governor and Sherrod Brown senator, but all the other statewide offices were still showing as red. Well, I just checked this morning, and holy buckets, every state office but auditor, including the Ohio Supreme Court seats, looks to have gone to the Democrats. By extremely small margins, to be sure! But you know what you call a win by an extremely small margin? A win.
And the US House races, with a new map that the state GOP designed to be gerrymandered as fuck to their advantage? Seven seats went to Democrats, which brings them to near parity with the GOP in a state with fifteen congressional districts. Shit, in my district, OH-8, Warren Davidson, who since 2016 has won his seat with between 60%-70% of the vote every election, scraped by this time with just 52% of the vote. The GOP nearly just gerrymandered themselves out of a state congressional majority. The GOP also looks to have lost its supermajority in the Ohio house, so, goodbye ignoring the governor’s veto for them. This is all excellent news.
As I noted the other day, and without taking away from the work of Acton, Brown and all the rest of the Democrats, it’s the fact the GOP voters, in their infinite wisdom, chose Vivek Ramaswamy as their candidate for governor in the primary, largely on the endorsement of Trump, that helped tip Ohio back into purplehood. It’s hard to overstate what a historically bad candidate Ramaswamy was, and ultimately how poor a fit he was for the Ohio GOP (much less any other Ohio voter). And even then he still got 44% of the vote, because tankies gonna tank. But 44% was not enough. So much for the power of a Trump endorsement in 2026.
Speaking of Trump, I have no doubt if the Democratic margins had been smaller this year that Trump would be doing his usual thing of belching about fixed elections and other such nonsense, but at the end of the evening the wave was high enough that even he couldn’t pretend that it was anything other than a wipeout. He rather meekly went on record that he would “respect the results” and then went on Truth Social to bluster that if he had been on the ballot things would have turned out differently. Motherfucker, you were on the ballot. Everything you’ve done in the last two years is why this election went the way it did.
I still expect Trump and his odious cronies to pull hijinks, and never forget that he is actually still president for two more years, unless he dies, resigns, is impeached, or just one day boards a plane for Russia just for fun and never comes back. We’re still stuck with him through January 2029. Adjust expectations accordingly.
But no matter what, last night was the beginning of the end of the Trump era. I’ve said such things before, mind you, and have been wrong. But I feel pretty good about this time. This wasn’t a normal election. Ask Texas about that. It’s not just a wave. It’s a sea change.
— JS

articles.title: Binance says hackers used fake job interviews and an internal AI tool to pull off the $6.3 billion heist
articles.body:
The largest crypto theft to date was pulled off by combining some well-known hacking techniques over the course of a few months, according to Binance. A postmortem from the company says the process started in June with one developer downloading a tampered installer apparently spread by a malicious Google ad, exposing details about the engineers and how they work. Then, in September, another engineer was targeted by someone pretending to be interested in hiring them; that person set up a series of calls and multiple rounds of interviews, shared social media pages to build trust, and eventually prompted them to download a fake interview assignment that was actually malware.
Binance says hackers used fake job interviews and an internal AI tool to pull off the $6.3 billion heist
A North Korean hacking unit reportedly started its break-in with a search engine ad that served up a malware download.
Binance claims that its security teams did detect the first installation of malware in June, and replaced the worker’s device, but that its security tools didn’t detect the second attack that deleted the pyenv executable and replaced it with a malicious version that gave them backdoor access:
The malware employed sophisticated obfuscation and evasion techniques, including replacing a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version to execute commands and establish communication with an attacker-controlled external server. The 0-day malware was not detected by the endpoint security protection tools at the time. The attacker also took steps to conceal the malicious activity and remove traces of the compromise, making detection and subsequent investigation more challenging.
By October 20th, the story goes, the attackers, whom the FBI has identified as a North Korean unit dubbed “TraderTraitor,” used Binance’s own internal AI tool to gain control over wallets for the first engineer compromised in June, as well as a third employee, before logging into the third employee’s computer on October 29th and launching their attack.
The postmortem also goes into why Binance wasn’t able to stop the transactions that occurred nearly two hours after the first unauthorized transfers, saying that “Because the hot wallet used Multi-Party Computation (MPC), there was no single private key that could be used to immediately revoke the malicious EIP-7702 authorizations.” Binance says that it has prevented 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threat cases, and CEO Richard Teng writes that no user is bearing the loss, with about $2.85 billion in stolen assets frozen or intercepted: “At this moment, 98% of impacted tokens had been replenished; we’re completing the remaining 2%. Withdrawals have broadly resumed.”
What’s less clear is why this particular attack worked — the danger of job interviews that ask people to download and execute code on machines with access to employer material has been warned about for years, and there’s little detail on the “internal AI tool” that was used by the attackers and why it was able to help them in the first place.

articles.title: EU Court Advisor Warns Google AI Chatbot May Breach Copyright Rules
articles.body:
EU Court Advisor Warns Google AI Chatbot May Breach Copyright Rules 21
			
		 	
				An adviser to the EU's highest court says Google's Gemini may violate publishers' copyright when it reproduces recognizable portions of their articles or circumvents paywalls and other technical protections to generate answers. Reuters reports:  The case before the Luxembourg-based Court of Justice of the European Union pitted Hungarian website operator Like Company against US-based Google's artificial intelligence chatbot Gemini. A ruling against Google, which could force the tech giant to pay fees for the use of such content, could throw a lifeline to online media such as Like Company. They have seen traffic dwindle as news summaries written by AI chatbots like Gemini increasingly replace traditional search engines' results, which include hyperlinks to the media websites.
"When an LLM (large language model)-driven chatbot retrieves a publication from a press publisher's website, reuses that publication to generate an answer, and provides that answer to the user, the press publisher's right may be infringed in certain circumstances," Advocate General Maciej Szpunar said. Gemini's answers fall under the publishers' right of reproduction when chatbots access publications by unlawfully "circumventing paywalls or other technical barriers, or when they reuse "the form of expression of that publication in a recognizable manner," he said.
Copyright rules do not protect the "mere facts" reported by press publications, but "only the specific form of expression," he added. On the other hand, he said, the use of material protected by copyright to train LLMs -- AI systems that use vast amounts of text to generate human-like responses and summarize information -- is "freely permitted under the text and data mining exception." Szpunar said there was no evidence that Google had used the Hungarian publisher's articles to train Gemini. The court, which follows the majority of its advisers' non-binding opinions, will rule in the coming months.  "Google's powerful gatekeeping role in search makes this particularly important. Publishers depend on Google to reach readers, while Google increasingly delivers AI-generated answers directly to users," said Angela Mills Wade, the council's executive director.
"Publishers should not have to choose between search visibility and protecting their rights. Nor should Google's control over access to audiences become leverage to secure publishers' content for AI services," she said.

articles.title: CrowdStrike to shell out nearly $500M for 2 AI security startups as the market for securing agents takes off
articles.body:
Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike is buying two AI security companies that expand its products to more broadly monitor, test, and cover AI models and agents, as companies across industries start rolling out AI agents and models wholesale.
CrowdStrike said it will buy Fiddler AI, which makes observability software for monitoring AI agents inside enterprises, and Dreadnode, which helps companies automate security testing specifically aimed at detecting flaws in AI models, apps, and agents before they are set live.
The company is paying around $400 million for Fiddler AI, and about $95 million for Dreadnode, according to The Wall Street Journal.
The deals are happening at a time of significant upheaval in the cybersecurity space, especially as companies’ policies and processes lag behind AI adoption within their walls. Teams and individual employees alike are experimenting with AI tools, automating workflows, vibe-coding custom apps, and deploying armies of AI agents to do their bidding, which is understandably causing headaches for security teams.
CrowdStrike, whose products are used widely across enterprises and governments, is clearly trying to leverage its already significant heft and presence to capture a share of this quickly burgeoning market. It’s not alone, of course, as we’ve already seen several startups and cybersecurity vendors raising dozens of millions in funding to solve issues for companies, though most of these approaches are essentially based on the conviction that existing security software isn’t enough to monitor and control AI tools, connectors, or usage.
The company has itself been building detection and response controls, dubbed Falcon Guardian, to help companies see and understand what agents are doing on their devices, and these acquisitions seem to further flesh out its offerings.
Fiddler AI is going to be part of CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform as Falcon Observe, where it’ll ostensibly help the company’s clients evaluate agents before they’re deployed, understand their actions, and monitor what they do, and feed that information as telemetry into the broader platform. Dreadnode, meanwhile, will be integrated into the Falcon Guardian product, to which the startup’s software will feed its testing results as security policy recommendations.
Founded in 2018, Fiddler AI has raised a total of about $99 million to date, according to PitchBook. Dreadnode, founded in 2023, has raised $14 million so far.

articles.title: I got banned from Lobsters for writing like an LLM
articles.body:
I got banned from Lobsters for writing like an LLM
I've been banned from Lobsters. If you're bored, you can read about my experience.
If you don't know it, Lobsters is a news aggregator focused on technology and computing, although other topics of general interest also come up. The most interesting part is the comments on each thread or link, where the topics are discussed. As alternatives, there are Hacker News, Lemmy and, to some extent, Reddit.
To give you some background, I've been a Lobsters user for a few years. I've contributed comments and links, and I'm also the author of the Emacs client. On top of that, the IRC channel I hang out in the most is #lobsters on Libera.Chat.
Chapter 1: Your domain has been blocked
A year ago, around Christmas 2025, I tried to share an article on Lobsters. My usual style, educational but fun. When I did, I ran into a warning telling me that my website's domain was blocked for self-promotion. My domain?
This surprised me, since I hadn't shared content from my website on Lobsters before, and I had read the odd unhappy comment. But blocking the whole domain seemed a bit much.
I didn't make a big deal of it! I sent an email to the moderators explaining the situation.
I got no reply.
Chapter 2: Contributing again
Almost a year later, with a few articles on the Hacker News front page, I thought about Lobsters again.
I decided to contribute again with a simple post: my experience building a modern BBS. Improvements over older systems like BBJ, and an explanation of some design decisions.
It ended with an invitation to try it, and I shared it with the show tag. Nothing more.
Same result: domain blocked for self-promotion. They hadn't lifted the block after a year, and they never answered my message.
I didn't make a big deal of it.
By chance, I found a way to post a blocked domain. It looked like a small bug.
I was posting again after a year in exile.
Chapter 3: The rise
Little by little, the points went up and the comments came in, nothing out of the ordinary. At 8 points I could see it on the front page.
I took my time to reply; the conversation was constructive. One user even found a design flaw. Fantastic! But... the joy didn't last long.
Soon after, the trouble started.
Chapter 4: Down the well
Several users accused me of using AI, not in my code but in my replies to the comments. One of them even included a link where an external service claimed that one of my replies was 100% AI-generated.
The evidence was irrefutable.
According to the tool, there wasn't the slightest doubt. I started to doubt my own self-awareness. What if I was an LLM and didn't know it?
Obviously I replied that it wasn't true (probably not). But the damage was done. Other users joined in with similar accusations, and the snowball kept rolling and getting bigger and bigger. They even called me a self-promotion bot! My existence had less and less dignity.
When I asked why they thought I was an LLM, I got a detailed explanation.
The number of users flagging the thread as spam kept growing. The situation became unsustainable.
The greyed-out, faded color means the thread has been hidden by many users.
If you try to open the thread now, you won't be able to unless you have an account. So how do I have screenshots? Well, that's a topic for another article.
I sent an urgent message to a moderator with the subject "Help!", along with a short explanation.
Again, I got no reply.
Some time later, with all hope lost, I saw a notification in the Lobsters menu. I had a new message, this time from a moderator.
Your story has been removed for breaking the community rules. Self-promotional content is not allowed.
My face was a picture when I read it.
It came with a link to the community rules, specifically this section:
Self-promotion: It's great to have authors participate in the community, but not to exploit it as a write-only tool for product announcements or driving traffic to their work. As a rule of thumb, self-promo should be less than a quarter of one's stories and comments in the last year. New users (first 70 days) are not allowed to submit self-promo.
Now I made a big deal of it!
I replied, asking where the fine line was between sharing knowledge and self-promotion, and whether there was any way to appeal the decision. The answer was that I had to improve my ratio of what they considered self-promotion.
Okay, I committed to it. I would write more comments and fewer links. It could be a discussion forum for me.
But the hardest blow was yet to come.
Chapter 5: Your account has been banned
Two hours later, I got the following message in my personal email:
Subject: [Lobsters] account X banned
You have been banned from Lobsters by ** ** ** For:
Only self-promo, slop.
You are no longer allowed to login to the site. If you wish, you can discuss this ban with the moderator by replying to this e-mail.
What happened? I thought the matter had been cleared up and settled.
I replied. I wasn't going to miss the chance to appeal the decision:
Hi *******,
I think there has been a misunderstanding.
[Here was an explanation of what happened]
[Here were my interactions with the moderators]
It has been an unfortunate situation, and I felt completely helpless.
At this point, could my account be reactivated? I don't think I'll find the courage to share more content after what happened, but I'd still like to contribute in the comments. I'm an active user on IRC. Also, I'd rather not live with the cognitive dissonance of maintaining an Emacs client for an aggregator/community I've been banned from.
Best regards
And the answer? The usual: silence, and nothing more.
Epilogue
Some questions are still on my mind. Will they be able to read me? If my domain is blocked, a regular user won't be able to submit this article, let alone comment on it (unless they use the same trick). Will they ever answer my messages? What would happen if I ran their own comments through the same AI detector?
On the other hand, it seems that writing long, detailed replies has become dangerous. Not long ago, when you took the time to write a careful text, with references or quotes, it was received with respect and admiration. Although you ran the risk of coming across as pretentious and pedantic. Today, however, the trend is short replies, without punctuation or embellishments. If you want to prove you're human, you have to write like a teenager chatting with their friends.
As for the moderation, I'm nobody to judge anyone. Who do you favor when there are problems? Individual users, or the group that contributes content and keeps the site alive? Maybe we would have done the same in their place, or maybe we would have tried to mediate. Who knows! There are also many variables we don't know. Still, silence is not pleasant.
If they lifted the ban, would I come back? Yes, but only to comment. My content fits better elsewhere, and that's fine. Every community has its own rules.
And for everything else... Hacker News, Reddit and other forums.

Help me keep writing
Every coffee gives me a push toward the next article.
