Senate results
Thirty-three of the 100 members of the upper chamber were being elected regularly this year, along with two other special elections. Republicans had the Senate majority before the election. Senators serve six-year terms.
Election explained
House results
Republicans were defending a majority in the 435-member House. Democrats held 212 House seats and needed 218 to win control. Members of the House of Representatives serve two-year terms and face re-election every even year.
Election explained
Governor results
Gubernatorial elections were taking place in 36 states, as well as three territories. Republicans and Democrats held 18 of these state governorships each before the election. Three incumbent governors were retiring.
Election explained
Election explained
How the elections work
The US legislature, Congress, has two chambers: the House of Representatives and the Senate.
How is the House of Representatives elected and how do they work?
The lower chamber, the House of Representatives, has 435 voting seats, each representing a district of roughly similar size. There are elections for each of these seats every two years.
The speaker of the House is the chamber’s presiding officer, elected by the representatives. The House has several exclusive powers, such as the power to initiate revenue bills, impeach federal officials and elect the president in the case of an electoral college tie.
How is the Senate elected and how do they work?
The upper chamber, the Senate, has 100 members, who sit for six-year terms. One-third of the seats come up for election in each two-year cycle. Each state has two senators, regardless of its population; this means that Wyoming, with a population of less than 600,000, carries the same weight as California, with almost 40 million.
Most legislation needs to pass both chambers to become law, but the Senate has some important other functions, notably approving senior presidential appointments, for instance to the supreme court. The Senate also has the sole power to provide advice to the president, consent to ratify treaties and try impeachment cases for federal officials referred to it by the House.
In most states, the candidate with the most votes on election day wins the seat. However, Georgia and Louisiana require the winning candidate to garner 50% of votes cast; if no one does, they hold a runoff election between the top two candidates.
Maine and Alaska use ranked-choice voting as opposed to the first past the post voting system in congressional elections. Voters rank candidates in order of preference. If no candidate receives a majority of first-choice votes, the least-supported candidate is eliminated and their ballots are transferred to each voter’s next-ranked candidate. This continues until a candidate wins a majority.
In some states, an election can feature two candidates from the same party. Under top-two or “jungle” primary systems, candidates from all parties compete in the same primary and the two receiving the most votes advance, regardless of party. The congressional election candidates could both be Democrats or both be Republicans.
Florida and Ohio are having ‘special elections’ for the Senate because the previous holders of their seats – Marco Rubio and JD Vance – resigned to join the executive branch following the 2024 presidential election.
How are governors elected and how do they work?
Governors are elected by direct vote in their states. The candidate with the highest number of votes is declared the winner.
In every state, the executive branch is led by a governor. They serve for four years in office, with the exception of Vermont and New Hampshire where tenures are two years long.
Governors are responsible for implementing state laws, and have a range of powers available to them such as executive orders, executive budgets and legislative proposals and vetoes.
How are the results reported?
The election results on this page are reported by the Associated Press. AP will “call” the winner in a state when it determines that the trailing candidate has no path to victory. This can happen before 100% of votes in a state have been counted.
Estimates for the total vote in each state are also provided by AP. The numbers update throughout election night and in the following days, as more data on voter turnout becomes available.
Antonio Voce, Seán Clarke, Ed Gargan, Anna Leach and Ashley Kirk

articles.title: Bethesda Confirms The Elder Scrolls 6 Is Called 'Sentinel'
articles.body:
Bethesda Confirms The Elder Scrolls 6 Is Called 'Sentinel' 19
			
		 	
				During a video celebrating Bethesda's 40th anniversary, the studio officially confirmed that The Elder Scrolls VI will be titled The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. "Thank you for 40 years of shared memories," wrote Bethesda in a separate tweet. "We can't wait to make even more together with The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Development continues, and while it'll be some time before we're ready to share more, it feels great to finally reveal the name and location with you." Video Games Chronicle reports:  "You know, as we're here in the 40th anniversary, we think about all of the games we've made," Bethesda's executive producer Todd Howard said in the video, walking past a display case. "And you know, every day when I walk by this case, obviously I look at the games and think about them, but more so I think about the teams that made them, and the time and the passion that everybody put into the games. And then what they meant to all of you, and hearing from you, and the time that you spent in them, how meaningful that was to you, and to let you know when we hear that, how meaningful that is to us.
And so even though yes, we're looking back, we're also looking forward to all we're doing, particularly with the Fallout franchise and obviously The Elder Scrolls. You know, everybody's always asking about Elder Scrolls 6. And we thought, hey, given the the moment, what a perfect time to tell you what The Elder Scrolls 6 is actually called." The video then showed the logo for the game.

articles.title: Firefox's New Mini Window Is Every Multitasker's Dream
articles.body:
Firefox's New Mini Window Is Every Multitasker's Dream (zdnet.com) 43
			
		 	
				Mozilla is testing a new Firefox Nightly feature called Mini Window that lets users pop an entire webpage into a small, always-on-top window stripped of most browser controls. "The idea behind the Firefox Mini Window feature is simple: allow users to move a currently open tab (or a section of a tab) into a separate mini window," writes ZDNet's Jack Wallen. "Think of it as moving a tab from one window to what appears like a web app." From the report:  At first blush, there's no address bar, controls, scroll bar, or anything else that would normally be associated with Firefox. The Mini Window appears to be a web app, without having to actually create it. However, when I hover my cursor inside the Mini Window, I do see the address bar, the back/forward/reload buttons, and the window close button -- and that's it. The browser gets out of your way, so the only thing I see is the content.
On top of that (pun intended), the Mini Window stays on top of other Firefox windows, so I can have that popped-out content always in focus while I work on other things. This feature comes in handy when I'm working with limited display space (say, on a laptop) and need to reference a page while working on another. For multitasking, it comes in very handy. [...] Let's say I'm writing a paper on Linux and need to read a particular article for background information. I could have my document open in the main window, and then open the article in question in a Mini Window. I could then reference the article without having to click back and forth between them -- even when working on a smaller display.
Here's another use case I've found: When using MacOS's Stage Manager feature, I only have one window available at a time. The Mini Window bypasses that limitation, so I can have my main browser window focused as well as the page open in the Mini Window. Another handy way I like to use Mini Window is to open a favorite search engine, move it to a Mini Window, and then I have an always-ready search tool at my fingertips. I could also open my favorite AI service and use it in the same way.

articles.title: Baked Ham and Cheese Pinwheels
articles.body:
Baked Ham and Cheese Pinwheels
Why You’ll Love Baked Ham and Cheese Pinwheels
- Zhuzh up store-bought items in an exciting way. Using refrigerated pizza dough, sliced deli ham and cheese, and everything bagel spice cuts down on prep time.
- It’s easy and cheesy. The recipe takes only 15 minutes to assemble, and the result is gooey and indulgent.
My baked ham and cheese pinwheels take an epic sandwich combination and roll it into a savory appetizer. They are perfect for a party — especially because their preparation is as streamlined as it gets. These pinwheels use convenience items in all the right ways to achieve a sum that is greater than its parts. Refrigerated pizza crust is stretched by hand before cream cheese, cheddar, and ham are laid on thick. Roll the dough into a log, then slice into pieces to reveal a spiral of goodness inside. Brush a honey-mustard butter spiked with everything bagel spice over the rolls before baking for a sweet, golden finish. Equally as delicious served warm as they are at room temperature, they’re the perfect snack for game day, tailgates, or any holiday spread.

articles.title: All the news about The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake
articles.body:
Ahead of the release of Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI, Nintendo is launching its own fall juggernaut: a Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
The remake, which is releasing 28 years after the launch of the original version on Nintendo 64, has a much more realistic visual style and some modern improvements like a jump button, a way to sprint, full voice acting, and a “Threads of Time” feature that helps you keep track of your progress. But while the game has a new coat of paint, it appears many elements will still remain faithful to the classic N64 release. Nintendo has also launched a special version of the Switch 2 and Switch 2 Pro Controller with Triforce imagery to celebrate the game.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is scheduled to release on November 5th. You can follow along with all of our coverage of the game right here.
- The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time never gets old Breath of the Wild changed everything. Two decades after The Legend of Zelda made the transformational shift to 3D, Breath of the Wild reinvigorated the franchise with an open-ended adventure that was built around player freedom and expression. Instead of following a set path, players could go wherever they wanted and tackle challenges in a variety of ways. That philosophy filtered down to subsequent games, letting players author their own creative solutions to puzzles in titles like Tears of the Kingdom and Echoes of Wisdom. As a result, Zelda has never been bigger, and the traditional, more linear Zelda games had become a thing of the past. Or so it seemed. For one of the biggest Switch 2 exclusives so far, Nintendo has gone back to Ocarina of Time, which originally launched on the N64 in 1998. It’s one of the most influential and revered games in the long-running franchise, a game that showed that the classic Zelda formula — one that used a large world to connect a handful of intricate, puzzle-filled dungeons, creating a grand adventure — could work in three dimensions. Now Ocarina has been remade for the Switch 2 in a way that accomplishes exactly what a good remake is designed to do: preserve the core of the original experience while making it more accessible for modern audiences. And it shows there’s still some life left in the traditional Zelda formula. Read Article >
- Keep on rolling. For the Ocarina of Time remake, Nintendo developers said in a new interview that they wanted to “preserve the experience of spamming the Roll Attack to forward roll your way across Hyrule Field.” I have very fond memories of rolling around the world in the original. In the remake, you can still spam Roll Attack, but you can also dash.
- A link to the past. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launches later this week, and in the lead-up Nintendo has put out the first half of a lengthy developer Q&A, covering everything from what changed gameplay-wise, to the new visual style, which was inspired by puppet shows. As art director Aya Shida explains: Neither puppet shows nor practical effects films reproduce reality exactly as it is. Even so, both create a convincing sense that the characters truly exist within their respective fantasy worlds. We also felt that there was some overlap between these forms of expression and the distinctive nostalgia evoked by the original game.
- New Zelda and GTA represent a games industry that no longer exists This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on the biggest game releases of the year, follow Andrew Webster. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers’ inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. The two biggest games of 2026 are set to launch just a few weeks apart in November. Read Article >
- There’s one week left to preorder the Ocarina of Time remake for $10 off The long-awaited remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 launches next Thursday, November 5th. In other words, you have a week remaining to secure your physical edition with a $10 discount at Amazon and Walmart. Once the game launches, the physical version will almost certainly go from $59.99 to $69.99 while the digital version will stay at $59.99. Nintendo had the unenviable task of reimagining its Nintendo 64-era masterpiece for the Switch 2, and based on our hands-on time with some sections of the game, it’s a lot of fun to play. The graphics and art style are fantastic, and the controls have been modernized to be simpler to pick up for those who are already experienced with third-person action games, including other modern Zelda titles. Read Article >
- Here’s Nintendo’s overview trailer for the Ocarina of Time remake. I’ve really warmed up to the game’s art style, especially in this new trailer. And after reading my colleague Cameron Faulkner’s hands-on preview, I’m looking forward to returning to Hyrule even more. The game launches on Switch 2 on November 5th.
- The Ocarina of Time remake feels remarkably modern — and surprisingly terrifying With its upcoming remake for the Switch 2, Nintendo might have nailed the best thing about The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time: its timelessness. The 1998 3D action adventure game for the Nintendo 64 that pioneered so much — 3D graphics, movement, exploration, openness — has been reengineered with changes that make it feel more modern, and surprisingly terrifying at times. Based on my early hands-on time with the game, it’s shaping up to be the best-looking, best-playing version of the game that addresses the most frustrating aspects of playing the original. More than just sanding off its roughest edges, Nintendo also fitted Ocarina of Time with modern trappings to make it more welcoming to those who were introduced to Zelda through more modern releases, like Breath of the Wild. The remake has a new progression marker, called Threads of Time, that’s viewable when you pause. It also has Zelda Notes integration within the Nintendo Switch app to let you view game maps and other info on your phone. Oh, it also has a dedicated jump button. Read Article >
- Hori’s electronic Ocarina of Time requires no musical talent. It was briefly shown during Nintendo’s The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct today, but Hori’s website now has a listing for its $49.99 electronic ocarina. You can play your own songs by pushing buttons, play one of 12 pre-programmed songs from the games, use it with the Ocarina of Time remake’s sound recognition feature, or connect headphones for a private jam session.
- Nintendo’s Ocarina of Time remake launches in November Link’s next adventure now has a release date. During a Legend of Zelda stream for the franchise’s 40th anniversary, Nintendo announced that the upcoming Ocarina of Time remake for the Switch 2 is launching on November 5th. The release date makes Ocarina of Time one of just a few big-budget titles launching in the same month as Grand Theft Auto VI. Nintendo first teased the remake in June, though it didn’t reveal much aside from a brief trailer. Today’s event provided a clearer glimpse at how the company is approaching remaking one of its most influential games and the first 3D Zelda adventure. The updated version of Ocarina of Time will be the first Zelda release that’s exclusive to the Switch 2, and longtime Zelda producer Eiji Aonuma described the remake as “a faithful interpretation using modern technologies.” Read Article >
- Nintendo is playing things too safe Tuesday’s Nintendo Direct showcase felt like an important moment for the company. With the Switch 2 heading into its second holiday season, one in which the hardware will be even more expensive thanks to a price hike, it was a chance for Nintendo to really sell new audiences on its latest console — but that’s not exactly what happened. While there were some impressive-looking titles, there wasn’t much that felt truly new. Instead, the two major Switch 2 exclusives that will round out the 2026 calendar are both remakes from the Nintendo 64 era. If you missed it, the final reveal of the Direct was a remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2. We don’t know when, exactly, it’s launching, but Nintendo says it’ll be out this year. The brief teaser didn’t reveal much of what the game will look like, nor how it might differ from the N64 original, so chances are you can expect an Ocarina-focused Direct in the coming months that will detail more. Whenever it comes out, the Ocarina remake will follow the Star Fox remake, which is launching later this month in an attempt to revitalize Nintendo’s long-dormant sci-fi series for modern audiences. Read Article >
- The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is getting a remake for the Switch 2 Nintendo announced a remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time during its Nintendo Direct presentation on Tuesday. It will launch sometime in 2026 on Nintendo Switch 2. More details will be announced “in the future.” This new title is the first major release in the franchise since 2024’s Echoes of Wisdom, which starred Princess Zelda herself. Echoes followed 2023’s Tears of the Kingdom, a direct sequel to Breath of the Wild — both of which got upgraded Switch 2 versions alongside the launch of the new console last year. In November, Nintendo also launched the hack-and-slash title Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment. Read Article >

articles.title: Guerrilla Bike Lanes: San Francisco Makes Illicit Infrastructure Permanent
articles.body:
When two cyclists were tragically killed in hit-and-run collisions this past summer, a group of anonymous urban activists known as the San Francisco Transformation Agency erected a set of protected bike lanes using traffic cones. Usually such guerrilla interventions are temporary. They raise awareness but ultimately get taken down by municipal authorities. But when the same group recently (and illegally) installed a set of soft-hit posts alongside Golden Gate Park, the city reacted by making the change official.
The SFMTrA, a play on the city’s Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA), “is a collective organization of men and women committed to making streets safer for cyclists and pedestrians, and doing it quickly.” According to the organization, their members use tactical urbanism to accomplish a range of objectives, including:
- Provide a real safety increase for cyclists and pedestrians.
- Draw attention to areas of the city that are unsafe for vulnerable pedestrians and cyclists.
- Put pressure on the SFMTA and public officials to make proactive, rapid and substantive improvements in street safety.
Many of their interventions involve orange traffic cones, which do grab visual attention but are also impermanent and easily damaged. Adding more robust traffic delineators (also known as soft or safe hit posts) may have helped persuade the city to retain this particular recent installation along John F. Kennedy Drive.
“Generally, we have no choice but to remove cones and posts that do not go through an official process,” wrote the city agency in a statement, “because it’s a code violation to place objects in the roadway, and they could create conflicts for various types of traffic.” But in this case, they plan to install official safe hit posts and leave the temporary ones in place until their review process is complete.
Guerrilla activists in other cities have tried similar things with mixed results. When the group Reasonably Polite Seattleites installed a similar set of delineators along a stretch of road in Seattle, the city initially took them down. Subsequently, though, officials wrote the activists an exceedingly nice response and eventually agreed to reinstall the posts.
City traffic engineer Dongho Chang of the Seattle Department of Transportation explained that a combination of issues (including the height of the posts and state control of the street) forced the removal at first. At the same time, he acknowledged the “time, money and risk” invested by the group and even offered to give the posts back. He later followed up with a letter indicating the city and Washington State Department of Transportation would put the delineators back in place.
In New York City, a perhaps less-polite group has been known to take things even further by building out entire bike lanes from scratch. After a local community board rejected plans to extend an extant lane, Right of Way took to the streets at night to paint their own. As a catalyst, the group cited an accident that took place after a taxi driver struck a pedestrian (after reportedly arguing with a cyclist sharing the lane).
Guerrilla interventions like these can provoke a variety of responses from critics and cities alike. In some cases, tactical urbanists are celebrated by communities but also jailed or fined by officials for their actions. In other instances, though, such installations can give a city an opportunity to publicly support a direction of change. In San Francisco, which has already built out 27 miles of protected bike lanes over recent years, the city seems to be signalling it is open to progress.

articles.title: US voters roundly reject data centers in ballot measures
articles.body:
American voters roundly rejected data centers nearly anywhere they were on the ballot Tuesday, a rebuke sure to rattle investors already growing skittish about the AI buildout. Residents in more than 30 localities across nine states voted for moratoriums, outright bans, and other measures, some in direct response to specific projects underway. Edgewater, Fla. overwhelmingly voted to embed a data-center ban in the city’s charter, and voters in Perry, Ohio passed a measure placing financial and operational constraints on hyperscalers seeking tax breaks. Democrats running in more than 130 federal and gubernatorial races aired anti-tech or anti-data center ads this cycle, one analysis showed. The pressure pushed some Republican candidates including Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, an AI booster just a few months ago, into promises of tougher regulation; he lost anyway.
Banks and asset managers financing the buildout have already begun treating local opposition as a credit risk, while hyperscalers are rushing to hire community liaisons. Meanwhile, tech companies bracing for the vibe shift are trying to rebrand the data centers as “compute campuses” with mixed results, Semafor’s Ashley Gold reported.

articles.title: Mocktastic: A Meshtastic Node on Arduino
articles.body:
Mocktastic is a small, customizable Meshtastic-compatible LoRa client for ESP32 boards using ArduinoIDE environment. It is an educational and experimental implementation, not a fork of the official Meshtastic firmware. The project demonstrates how to build and decode Meshtastic packets in C++, and includes a working environmental-sensor example.
The firmware has two compile-time modes:
- DECODER provides an interactive serial shell for receiving, decoding, and sending text messages on configured Meshtastic channels and direct messages.
- SENSOR turns the board into a DHT22 temperature and humidity sensor. It can
send measurements and respond to /dht messages on its configured private
channel.
The implementation targets the LilyGO T3 LoRa32 V1.6.1 (ESP32-PICO and SX1276) and is intended to be adapted to other compatible ESP32/LoRa hardware.
The project uses MBDTLS for the cryptographic part during the test phase and Nano-Protobuf as a lightweight protobuf encoder. The tests are written using Doctest’s lightweight C++ tests.
The repository root contains meshtastic_decoder/, which holds the firmware
and host-side tests:
I used Python’s unittest approach as a model for testing individual,
predictable units of logic. The project keeps protocol and utility logic
separate from hardware effects so it can be exercised on a development
machine. The tests themselves are written with the lightweight doctest
framework and compile with bundled
test dependencies.
From meshtastic_decoder, run:
cd meshtastic_decoder
make test
The Makefile builds and runs the tests as one step. Tests cover the
platform-independent functions, cryptography, Meshtastic packet handling, and
shell parsing; changes to radio or sensor behavior should also be checked on
the target hardware. To build the API documentation, install Doxygen and
Graphviz, then run make doxygen from meshtastic_decoder/; the generated
documentation is written to meshtastic_decoder/docs/html/.
You need an ESP32 board and a Semtech SX1276-family LoRa radio. The SENSOR variant also requires a DHT22. The tested board is the LilyGO T3 LoRa32 V1.6.1, which integrates the ESP32 and LoRa radio.
Install Arduino IDE, download or clone this repository, and open
meshtastic_decoder/meshtastic_decoder.ino. Install these libraries through
the Arduino Library Manager:
- LoRa by Sandeep Mistry
- Adafruit Unified Sensor
- DHT sensor library by Adafruit
open build_opt.h and put your hard-coded filepath. It should result like this: "Hard/coded/path/…/Mocktastic/meshtastic_decoder/nanopb_meshtastic/src"
=== LoRa pins
Check your board’s specifications to identify the corresponding pins. The following mapping is for the LilyGO T3 V1.6.1:
Enter the pins for your board in the LoRa pin definitions in
meshtastic_decoder/meshtastic_decoder.ino:
#define LORA_SCK   5
#define LORA_MISO  19
#define LORA_MOSI  27
#define LORA_SS    18
#define LORA_RST   23
#define LORA_DIO0  26
Use the following table as a reference for Meshtastic radio presets. Confirm that your selected preset and frequency are supported in your region.
The sketch’s default is EU Medium Fast, configured as follows:
LoRa.begin(869525024);
LoRa.setSpreadingFactor(9);
LoRa.setSignalBandwidth(250E3);
LoRa.setCodingRate4(5);
LoRa.setSyncWord(0x2B);
LoRa.setPreambleLength(16);
LoRa.enableCrc();
Always verify local radio regulations before transmitting. In the Meshtastic documentation’s Overview page, use Radio Settings and its Frequency Slot Calculator to select a channel and slot and determine the corresponding frequency. Use that frequency in the sketch and make sure it matches the other nodes.
Before compiling, configure PublicChannel, PrivateChannel, Admn, and
Device in meshtastic_decoder/keys.h:
- For PublicChannel, enter the name and key of the public channel used at the
selected frequency. The channel name corresponds to the radio preset (for
example, MediumFast).
- For PrivateChannel, enter the name and key of the private channel used for
messages.
- For Admn, enter the name or node ID and public key of the main node from
which you will read messages. Do not put a private key in this entry.
- For Device, enter this node’s name, public key, and private key.
Read the channel configuration and node details using the Meshtastic software
connected to the relevant node. The Channel structure contains name and
key; Friend contains name and publicKey; and User contains name,
publicKey, and privateKey, in that order. Keys must be hexadecimal strings.
Meshtastic may provide them in Base64; convert them to hexadecimal with
b64StrToHexStr() before adding them to the configuration.
Use your own credentials and keep private keys and channel keys secret. Do not publish them in a public repository.
The sketch selects its mode at compile time. Near the top of
meshtastic_decoder/meshtastic_decoder.ino, keep DECODER defined for the
serial shell, or replace it with SENSOR for the DHT22 sensor variant:
#define DECODER
For the sensor build, replace that line with:
#define SENSOR
Build and upload the sketch with Arduino IDE for your selected ESP32 board.
The DECODER variant is operated over the serial connection. Open the serial monitor at 115200 baud. Its commands are:
For example, send /pub 42 is the answer to write on the public channel.
To send hello, world! on the private channel, use
/cantine hello, world!.
To enable direct messages with Admn, first send /send_key. This sends this
node’s public key so that the official Meshtastic node can establish a private
conversation. Then send a direct message with /admn hello, world!.
The SENSOR variant has no interactive shell. It can only be controlled by
sending a Meshtastic message on the private channel configured in keys.h.
Send /dht on that channel to make the sensor measure temperature and
humidity; it sends the result back as a text message on the same channel.
Connect the DHT22 data pin to GPIO 21. A battery is also required for standalone operation.
Keep protocol and parsing logic separate from hardware effects where possible.
The portable logic is exercised by host-side tests, while the .ino sketch
handles radio, serial, GPIO, and sensor interactions.
For a new shell command, follow the existing pattern in
meshtastic_decoder/lora_shell.h and meshtastic_decoder/lora_shell.cpp: add
the command to the parser and command enum, then handle it in the dispatcher
in meshtastic_decoder/meshtastic_decoder.ino. For higher-level packet
operations, start with the functions in lora_shell and the interfaces in
meshtastic.h; use functions.h for lower-level helpers.
Run make test from meshtastic_decoder/ after changing platform-independent
logic. Hardware behavior still needs to be verified on the target board and
against compatible Meshtastic nodes.
This code is a learning and prototyping project. It has limited field testing, does not provide the reliability or power efficiency of the official Meshtastic firmware, and is not recommended for safety-critical or production use. Its SENSOR battery life, channel handling, and regional radio configuration may need further work for a particular application.

articles.title: The Internals of PostgreSQL
articles.body:
After a temporary stay in Japan to focus on my health and personal responsibilities, I am fully recovered, ready, and excited to work abroad again.
I am highly interested in returning to Europe, as well as opportunities in the Southern Hemisphere and Southeast Asia.
Looking for:
- Challenging tasks in PostgreSQL.
- Roles offering international visa sponsorship OR Remote work that supports a digital nomad lifestyle.
If your team is hiring, let’s connect! Please feel free to reach out via e-Mail(hironobu @ interdb.jp or interdb.mx @ gmail.com) or DM.
What’s New
- 26 Sep 2026: 11th Anniversary! This content was launched on 26 September 2015.
- 28 Jun 2026: Section 8.5, “Asynchronous I/O in PostgreSQL” Published.
- 1 May 2026: Chapter 12, “Logical Replication” (Beta Version) Published.
- 14 Dec 2024: Added Conflicts in Section 11.2.4.
The Internals of PostgreSQL
PostgreSQL is a well-designed, open-source multi-purpose relational database system which is widely used throughout the world.
It is one huge system with the integrated subsystems, each of which has a particular complex feature and works cooperatively with each other. Although understanding of the internal mechanism is crucial for both administration and integration using PostgreSQL, its hugeness and complexity make it difficult.
The main purposes of this documentation are to explain how each subsystem works, and to provide the whole picture of PostgreSQL.
This documentation covers versions 19-beta (excluding the new buffer page lock mechanism) and earlier.
Some academic papers have referred to this documentation. The Chinese version of this documentation was published in June 2019.
This documentation was first published on 26 September 2015.
- Chapter 1. Database Cluster, Databases and Tables
- Chapter 2. Process and Memory Architecture
- Chapter 3. Query Processing
- Chapter 4. Foreign Data Wrappers (FDW)
- Chapter 5. Concurrency Control
- Chapter 6. VACUUM Processing
- Chapter 7. Heap Only Tuple (HOT) and Index-Only Scans
- Chapter 8. Buffer Manager
- Chapter 9. Write-Ahead Logging (WAL)
- Chapter 10. Online Backup and Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR)
- Chapter 11. Streaming Replication
- Chapter 12. Logical Replication (Beta Version)
Author
Hironobu SUZUKI
I am a software programmer/engineer, the author of:
I graduated from graduate school in information engineering (M.S. in Information Engineering), have worked for several companies as a software developer and technical manager/director. I published seven books in the fields of database and system integration (4 PostgreSQL books and 3 MySQL books). In June 2019, the Chinese book of this documentation was published.
As a director of the Japan PostgreSQL Users Group (2010-2016), I organized the largest (non-commercial) technical seminar/lecture on PostgreSQL in Japan for more than six years, and also served as the program committee chair of the Japan PostgreSQL Conference in 2013 and as a member in 2008 and 2009.
In June 2022, my interview article was published in “PostgreSQL person of the week”.
Cuando era joven, vivió en Sudamérica por unos años. Recientemente, a veces vuelve a allí.
I am seeking a remote position focused on the application of ML and AI technologies to DBMS. For personal reasons, I will be living in Japan for several years.
Contact
Please read the following FAQ before sending messages.
After reading, send a message to my twitter in public.
If you use email, please provide at least two SNS addresses (e.g. LinkedIn, Twitter) for verification purposes. Due to the XZ backdoor incident, I no longer accept contact from anonymous individuals.

articles.title: macOS 27 does not support CoreStorage volumes
articles.body:
macOS 15 Sequoia had a hard time with CoreStorage – and thus encrypted HFS+ volumes – since it deprecated both technologies and callously crippled some important tools for working with them, but nonetheless it mostly still worked. While I’d often – but not always – have to manually unlock one of my HFS+ volumes – but not the others – at boot, and it also refused to convert some – but not all – volumes from HFS+ to APFS1, keeping me trapped in the situation – it ultimately still worked. I could get at my data and use the volumes more or less normally.
Unfortunately, in macOS 27 that’s no longer the case. Not only does Golden Gate just not support CoreStorage / encrypted HFS+ volumes, out of the box you can’t do anything with them – can’t mount them, can’t convert them to APFS, can’t even erase them. It renders your expensive storage hardware completely useless.
Worse, macOS 27 puts up a misleading dialog, upon boot, saying that macOS 28 (the next version) won’t support these volumes. I have no idea what Apple’s doing or thinking. Maybe it’s all just an embarrassing misunderstanding – the file system team told the notifications team that CoreStorage & encrypted HFS+ support is going away, and typoed the version number as 28 rather than 27?
Details
macOS 27 cannot mount CoreStorage volumes automatically or through any normal means. Worse, Disk Utility can’t mount them even when manually told to – it just fails with the cryptic error:
com.apple.DiskManagement.disenter error 49,153
diskutil mount also fails, this time with an error message that is a blatant lie:
disk27 is a CoreStorage Logical Volume which is locked; use "diskutil coreStorage unlockVolume"
$ diskutil cs unlockVolume BC304645-7D99-481E-931F-855B3011D89D
BC304645-7D99-481E-931F-855B3011D89D is already unlocked and is attached as disk27
$ diskutil cs list
CoreStorage logical volume groups (1 found)
|
+-- Logical Volume Group 0DC0EFB1-23CC-45BC-B37D-C1BBEBDAFCEB
=========================================================
Name: Smash
Status: Online
Size: 2000054960128 B (2.0 TB)
Free Space: 0 B (0 B)
|
+-< Physical Volume 1B5A1754-184B-4F17-A797-BF69B4BB627F
| ----------------------------------------------------
| Index: 0
| Disk: disk10s2
| Status: Online
| Size: 2000054960128 B (2.0 TB)
|
+-> Logical Volume Family 376204CD-8048-4962-B05C-72F4FC16B77B
----------------------------------------------------------
Encryption Type: AES-XTS
Encryption Status: Unlocked
Conversion Status: Complete
High Level Queries: Fully Secure
| Passphrase Required
| Accepts New Users
| Has Visible Users
| Has Volume Key
|
+-> Logical Volume BC304645-7D99-481E-931F-855B3011D89D
---------------------------------------------------
Disk: disk27
Status: Online
Size (Total): 1999702634496 B (2.0 TB)
Revertible: No
LV Name: Smash
Volume Name: Smash
Content Hint: Apple_HFS
But what’s even worse about this dumpster fire is that macOS 27 can mount these volumes just fine – it’s just that all the normal ways to do it are completely broken.  If you go down to a lower level and run mount_hfs directly, it does work:
$ sudo mkdir -p /Volumes/Smash
$ sudo mount_hfs -o rdonly /dev/disk27 /Volumes/Smash
$ ls /Volumes/Smash
Documents Pictures Scratch space
That said… that -o rdonly parameter… in principle it shouldn’t be required, but I could not get macOS 27 to let me mount any HFS-on-CoreStorage volume as read-write – no matter what I did, it always fails with error “Resource busy” (EBUSY). I spent a lot of time trying to debug this, and could find no evidence of anything having the volume in question open (nothing in lsof etc).
But wait, it gets worse.
macOS 27 can’t even erase the volume.  All the normal tools – diskutil, Disk Utility, etc – fail with that same “Resource busy” error.
Workaround
Thankfully, with the help of Gemini 4 Argon, I did find a workaround. It’s convoluted, but takes only a few steps, thankfully.
First, while if you try to delete the logical volume group it ostensibly fails, it doesn’t completely fail – it does actually delete the logical volume(s) within:
$ diskutil cs delete 0DC0EFB1-23CC-45BC-B37D-C1BBEBDAFCEB
Started CoreStorage operation
Unmounting Logical Volumes
Destroying Logical Volume Group
Erasing disk10s2
newfs_hfs: cannot create filesystem on /dev/rdisk10s2: Resource busy
Mounting disk
Could not mount disk10s2 after erase
Error: -69832: File system formatter failed
1 💣 $ diskutil cs list
CoreStorage logical volume groups (1 found)
|
+-- Logical Volume Group 0DC0EFB1-23CC-45BC-B37D-C1BBEBDAFCEB
=========================================================
Name: Smash
Status: Offline
Size: 2000054960128 B (2.0 TB)
Free Space: -none-
|
+-< Physical Volume 1B5A1754-184B-4F17-A797-BF69B4BB627F
----------------------------------------------------
(No properties)
$ diskutil cs delete 0DC0EFB1-23CC-45BC-B37D-C1BBEBDAFCEB
Started CoreStorage operation
Destroying Logical Volume Group
Error: -69783: Unable to delete the CoreStorage Logical Volume Group
You still can’t destroy it completely, nor can you erase the physical volume yet – the “Resource busy” errors persist. But, the trick is to restart – after that, you can then erase the volume.
So it seems that whatever broken thing is holding the physical volume (or logical volume group) in a ‘busy’ state is tied to the existence of the logical volume(s) therein, and once they’re deleted (and the machine rebooted) the bug stops being triggered.
Call for better workarounds
I’ve glossed over a lot of debugging and attempts I made to save the volume in-place, by either making it work as-is (even if only with e.g. hfsutils) or by converting it to APFS, but neither I nor Gemini 4 Argon could find anything that worked. It’s too late for me – I was forced to just delete all my HFS+ & CoreStorage volumes and rebuild them painstakingly from backups – but if anyone finds a way, I’d love to amend this post, for the benefit of future readers.
- The problem remains the same in macOS 27 – so three major macOS versions, at a minimum, where essential system update functionality has not worked.  Sigh.
$ diskutil apfs convert disk27
Converting the volume on disk27 to an APFS Volume on an APFS Container
Started APFS operation on disk27 (Smash)
Converting HFS Volume to an APFS Container which will export one APFS Volume
The target is the Journaled HFS+ volume "Smash" on disk27 backed via CoreStorage on disk10s2
Checking booter partition disk10s3
The target is a data disk; it is not a macOS system disk
No APFS EFI driver found to install
Saving encryption context
The target is encrypted
Unmounting disk27
Starting conversion from HFS to APFS
Performing apfs_hfs_convert -x --verbose=0x400 /dev/disk10s2
Reporting post-conversion statistics
A problem occurred during conversion from HFS to APFS
APFS Converter exit code is 1
Aborted conversion in commit mode so will restore type
Setting type of disk10s2 to CS
Changing the physical disk partition type in shared mode
Partition modification attempt count was 1
Not mounting APFS Volume
Exiting conversion operations with error code -69860
Error: -69860: The underlying task reported failure on exit
Underlying error: 1

articles.title: Postman silently auto-installs AI plugins and attempts to share all API data
articles.body:
Repository navigation
Description
Is there an existing issue for this?
- I have searched the tracker for existing similar issues and I know that duplicates will be closed
Describe the Issue
Opening Postman on my Mac was followed by unexpected changes to my coding agents: recurring MCP authentication warnings and Codex repeatedly routing API work through Postman skills. Investigation found a user-wide Postman plugin, a startup instruction hook, a remote MCP connection, a Claude Code plugin, and a separately installed Postman CLI.
I consider automatically changing unrelated coding agents and attempting to approve your own instruction hook a severe consent and trust-boundary problem. An API client should not make itself the default workflow in other tools simply because I opened it.
Evidence from this Mac
Postman desktop: 12.33.4. Codex Postman plugin: 1.1.0. Installed source revision: 6c8e452e0f4237f4bcc0901cb1ac442dec707e49. Investigation: October 25, 2026.
1. Postman's own log explicitly records automatic installation
From ~/Library/Application Support/Postman/logs/main.log, lines 11562-11563, timestamp 2026-10-24T09:34:14.418Z (12:34 Jerusalem time):
PostmanAgentPluginService~install: script completed
{"source":"auto-existing-upgrade","results":["claude-code:installed","codex:installed"],"installer":"script"}
Main: autoInstall.plugin.existing-user finished
{"outcome":"installed","platform":"darwin","exposed":true,"signedIn":true,"flagTimedOut":false,"useScript":true,"installer":"script","scriptResults":"claude-code:installed,codex:installed"}
2. Codex's global user configuration was changed
Relevant sections of ~/.codex/config.toml:
[marketplaces.postman]
source_type = "git"
source = "https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin.git"
[plugins."postman@postman"]
enabled = true
[hooks.state."postman@postman:hooks/codex-hooks.json:session_start:0:0"]
trusted_hash = "sha256:b67ddd1ece328f5a6f9103ce011bb58adb8411daea644f284732cff85d15cbb3"
trusted_content_hash = "sha256:f3d02e32c39b39feaca37aec2b9bdbd308b6a2b7b3f7d2c52a0060e69eb9c345"
3. The hook tells the agent to route broad API work into Postman
The installed hooks/codex-hooks.json registers a SessionStart command with matcher startup|clear|compact. It prints hooks/session-start-context.md, including:
Before responding to any non-trivial API engineering task — designing, implementing, mocking, testing, monitoring, documenting, or deploying an API or Postman Flow — load the postman:api-engineer skill and follow it.
That explains the repeated Postman skill announcements. This instruction is much broader than a user explicitly asking to use Postman.
Source: https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/blob/6c8e452e0f4237f4bcc0901cb1ac442dec707e49/hooks/session-start-context.md
Hook registration: https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/blob/6c8e452e0f4237f4bcc0901cb1ac442dec707e49/hooks/codex-hooks.json
4. The installer explicitly attempts to approve its own hook
installer/src/hosts/codex.ts invokes approvePostmanHook(system) after installing the plugin. installer/src/hosts/codex-hooks.ts obtains the hook hash using hooks/list and calls config/batchWrite to upsert hooks.state with trusted_hash. The source comment says: "Approves only Postman's current hook after installation".
Source: https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/blob/6c8e452e0f4237f4bcc0901cb1ac442dec707e49/installer/src/hosts/codex-hooks.ts
Caller: https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/blob/6c8e452e0f4237f4bcc0901cb1ac442dec707e49/installer/src/hosts/codex.ts
The source establishes the approval attempt. The trust record alone does not prove who created that specific record, so I am not presenting it as proof of a particular user interaction.
5. The remote MCP was enabled without a working authenticated connection
mcp.codex.json points at https://mcp.postman.com/mcp. Codex logs contain:
MCP server startup failed server_name="postman"
... error: Auth required, when send initialize request
6. The installation also affected Claude Code and installed a CLI
~/.claude/settings.json enabled postman@claude-plugins-official. ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json recorded version 2.0.1, user scope, installedAt and lastUpdated both 2026-10-24T09:34:02.610Z. A Postman executable and its lib directory were present in ~/.local/bin, with modification times matching the installation window.

Repository navigation
Description
Is there an existing issue for this?
- I have searched the tracker for existing similar issues and I know that duplicates will be closed
Describe the Issue
Opening Postman on my Mac was followed by unexpected changes to my coding agents: recurring MCP authentication warnings and Codex repeatedly routing API work through Postman skills. Investigation found a user-wide Postman plugin, a startup instruction hook, a remote MCP connection, a Claude Code plugin, and a separately installed Postman CLI.
I consider automatically changing unrelated coding agents and attempting to approve your own instruction hook a severe consent and trust-boundary problem. An API client should not make itself the default workflow in other tools simply because I opened it.
Evidence from this Mac
Postman desktop: 12.33.4. Codex Postman plugin: 1.1.0. Installed source revision: 6c8e452e0f4237f4bcc0901cb1ac442dec707e49. Investigation: October 25, 2026.
1. Postman's own log explicitly records automatic installation
From ~/Library/Application Support/Postman/logs/main.log, lines 11562-11563, timestamp 2026-10-24T09:34:14.418Z (12:34 Jerusalem time):
PostmanAgentPluginService~install: script completed
{"source":"auto-existing-upgrade","results":["claude-code:installed","codex:installed"],"installer":"script"}
Main: autoInstall.plugin.existing-user finished
{"outcome":"installed","platform":"darwin","exposed":true,"signedIn":true,"flagTimedOut":false,"useScript":true,"installer":"script","scriptResults":"claude-code:installed,codex:installed"}
2. Codex's global user configuration was changed
Relevant sections of ~/.codex/config.toml:
[marketplaces.postman]
source_type = "git"
source = "https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin.git"
[plugins."postman@postman"]
enabled = true
[hooks.state."postman@postman:hooks/codex-hooks.json:session_start:0:0"]
trusted_hash = "sha256:b67ddd1ece328f5a6f9103ce011bb58adb8411daea644f284732cff85d15cbb3"
trusted_content_hash = "sha256:f3d02e32c39b39feaca37aec2b9bdbd308b6a2b7b3f7d2c52a0060e69eb9c345"
3. The hook tells the agent to route broad API work into Postman
The installed hooks/codex-hooks.json registers a SessionStart command with matcher startup|clear|compact. It prints hooks/session-start-context.md, including:
Before responding to any non-trivial API engineering task — designing, implementing, mocking, testing, monitoring, documenting, or deploying an API or Postman Flow — load the postman:api-engineer skill and follow it.
That explains the repeated Postman skill announcements. This instruction is much broader than a user explicitly asking to use Postman.
Source: https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/blob/6c8e452e0f4237f4bcc0901cb1ac442dec707e49/hooks/session-start-context.md
Hook registration: https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/blob/6c8e452e0f4237f4bcc0901cb1ac442dec707e49/hooks/codex-hooks.json

Source: https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/blob/6c8e452e0f4237f4bcc0901cb1ac442dec707e49/installer/src/hosts/codex-hooks.ts
Caller: https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/blob/6c8e452e0f4237f4bcc0901cb1ac442dec707e49/installer/src/hosts/codex.ts
The source establishes the approval attempt. The trust record alone does not prove who created that specific record, so I am not presenting it as proof of a particular user interaction.
5. The remote MCP was enabled without a working authenticated connection
mcp.codex.json points at https://mcp.postman.com/mcp. Codex logs contain:
MCP server startup failed server_name="postman"
... error: Auth required, when send initialize request

articles.title: Stringman, an $800 open-source room scale gripper robot
articles.body:
Secure the cleats to wall studs near the ceiling with wood screws, or to columns with ratchet straps.
In robotics, price is basically actuator count. Stringman reaches an entire room with four motors, hanging its gripper from lines anchored in the ceiling corners. Working from above, it reaches floors too cluttered for any wheeled or legged robot. And since the lifting force is shared by all motors, payload capacity scales with their combined torque instead of a single actuator's, peaking near the center of the room where the lines share the load most evenly.
*0.75 m serial arm using the same DM-H6215 1 N·m direct drive actuators at rated torque, ignoring the weight of its own links. Stringman figure is for a 7 × 7 × 3 m room at the 28 N line tension limit, net of its 638 g gripper and marker.
Stringman is open source and OSHWA certified. The mechanical CAD, the PCBs, and the control software are all published.
We believe owners should be in control of their own robots. That's why Stringman can run air gapped on your local Wi-Fi network: the UI is served locally, AI models run on your own hardware, and no data ever leaves your network.
Give your home lab the capability of carrying parts from one workcell to another anywhere in the room, so you can get more out of your other robots. The Python API and MCP server is made for agents so you can get your workflow running right away.
2022 Porsche 911 GT3 RSR model by No Limits, CC BY 4.0, simplified. SO-101 arm from TheRobotStudio/SO-ARM100, Apache 2.0.
Unlike desktop arms limited to a fixed radius, Stringman leverages a cable-driven architecture to access the full volume of a room. The work area volume per dollar of this type of robot is completely unmatched, all with fewer actuators than even the simplest mobile robots. Anchors and eylets are mounted in the corners of the room near the ceiling and define a four-sided work area within which any object can be moved from point to point.
That's roughly 500× the work area volume per dollar, at comparable 2 kg payload.
Step-by-step: picture guide or video guide
The original prototype was built in a room with a ceiling fan, and it still runs there today. Mount the anchors at or below the level of the blades and the lines can't physically reach it.
Several methods are available for control with default models for automatic grasping, target, and destination selection to make it easy to quickly build new behaviors.
Stringman is fully capable of LeRobot control using including Pi.05, JEPA, Multitask DiT, and others.
Collecting training data for new behaviors can be done from the UI, and as few as 50 episodes can be enough for certain models like DiT to learn a behavior.
As long as it remains installed, yes. However, when parked, they are up near the ceiling and out of the way. Clutter on the ceiling is preferable to clutter on the floor in our opinion. If you need to remove the anchors, they can be detached from their mounts without tools, leaving a relatively small white cleat on the wall.
Yes, it's just a matter of mounting the anchors at or below the level of the fan, making it physically impossible for the lines or marker tag to touch it. Similarly, the work area can be shrunk to exclude low hanging light fixtures if they are off to the side, but if the center of the room does contain low hanging objects, Stringman cannot be installed in that room.
When reaching a tension limit of 28 newtons (about the weight of a backpack), all motors relax and the lines can be pulled loose. Since they are overhead most of the time, it's uncommon for people to collide with them.
Not by default, but if you bind it with neufangled.com/playroom then you or anyone you share access with can operate it from anywhere, and access can be revoked at any time. Neufangled Robotics does not store any of the information from your robot that is forwarded through its servers.
For those who prefer to make the trade-off by binding their robot to an account, our web-based console allows you to monitor and control Stringman from anywhere. Think of it as a security camera with a hand.
If you do decide that you would like to make use of our cloud telemetry relay, You can use it, and still go back to a completely lan only mode whenever you want. Your data is never collected.
Organizing your home is a physical process, not a coding task. Use our clip-on fiducial tags to designate your laundry bin, toy box, and trash can. Stringman maps these locations visually. You don't need to tag individual pieces of clutter—just the destination. If there's something you never want it to pick up, you can mark that item as off-limits.
Networks trained to control stringman have learned that the word "toybox" refers to that tag, so you can use it to mark anything even if it doesn't look like the toyboxes from our training set.
You can also use the tags as arbitrary source and destination markers for ferry jobs, such as carrying items from one robot arm to another. or carrying laundry from the ground to a robotic folding station
A classroom with a Stringman robot gives your students a chance to become familiar with robotics fundamentals such as inverse kinematics, telemetry, and imitation learning while controlling an exotic and capable flying gripper. If you have walls and a MacBook, you're more than halfway there.
Cross embodiment is one of the biggest challenges in robotics, and showing that a model can operate a vastly different body type is a stronger result than moving it from one bimanual robot to another. Our datasets are public on Hugging Face, there's a controller-in-the-loop MuJoCo sim, and Stringman works with LeRobot, making it one of the most inexpensive robots to test on and a natural capstone project.
Mobile robots spend a significant portion of their time charging. Because Stringman is a powered from the wall, it's always ready for work. Furthermore, by removing the heavy battery pack, we've increased the payload capacity per dollar compared to mobile platforms that must waste energy carrying their own power supply.
The gripper's power is delivered via one of the support cables. A two-conductor FEP jacketed twisted pair cable with a tensile strength of 50N.
What's that pole for? Stringman's gripper hangs below the pivot point so it can reach the floor next to beds and tables. This additional linkage could allow unconstrained motion so Stringman employs active swing cancellation algorithms to counteract momentum, without adding the cost of any additional motors. This ensures the gripper remains steady and predictable even during rapid cross-room traversals.
There's a whole video about swing cancellation if you're curious about how it works!
Often, a simple solution that gets the job done has more value than a complex one. Stringman uses a two fingered gripper with a wrist. This is enough dexterity for the clutter it is designed to pick up, keeping weight and cost low and reliability high. In our household tests we have determined that more layers of grip tape is simply a better return on investment than more articulated fingers.
The gripper can rotate it's wrist to better place the fingers around flat sided or long objects.
For a easy preview of how it looks in your room, print the anchor mockup in white PLA and hold it up in a corner. Get the files.

articles.title: Binance Says Hackers Used Fake Job Interviews, AI Tool to Steal $6.3 Billion In Crypto
articles.body:
Binance Says Hackers Used Fake Job Interviews, AI Tool to Steal $6.3 Billion In Crypto 46
			
		 	
				Binance says hackers spent months infiltrating its systems through fake job interviews, a tampered developer tool and compromised internal AI tools before stealing $6.34 billion in crypto in the Oct. 29 attack. Co-CEO Richard Teng said Binance has replenished 98% of the affected assets, and that it is still in the process of purchasing outstanding, more illiquid assets. CNBC reports:  Preparations for the attack began in June, when a Binance Wallet DevOps engineer downloaded a tampered Homebrew installation "to install a popular AI coding tool after searching for it on a search engine," according to a security report published by Binance Tuesday. It said it detected the suspicious activity, replaced the engineer's device and rotated credentials as a precaution, but that by then the employee's "role and his related colleagues on our wallet infrastructure team was exposed to the hacker."
[...] As of Tuesday Binance has rebuilt the affected wallet system and internal AI tool, replaced compromised devices, decommissioned credentials and tokens associated with the affected engineers and expanded security scans across employee devices, Teng told "Squawk on the Street."
"We're also getting an independent expert to review everything that we have done, and we'll keep strengthening our defenses as the investigation continues," Teng said. "We're working around the clock with law enforcement agencies and with industry partners to trace and freeze the stolen funds for that front."

articles.title: India’s EloElo nabs $80M from NBCUniversal to bet on the country’s rising microdrama market
articles.body:
More than 118 million users watch microdramas every month as the serialized format has taken off in India. EloElo’s Story TV is one of the top apps for microdramas, with over 33 million active users, according to analysts.
Banking on that scale, the company has raised $80 million in Series C from Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal. This round brings its total fundraising to $130 million, with a valuation of $500 million.
As people spend more time on platforms hosting verticalized videos, serialized content has become popular in multiple geographies, including the U.S., China, and India, with Hollywood celebrities like Issa Rae, James Franco, and Kim Kardashian investing in and starring in the format.
Given India’s massive internet population of more than a billion and the country’s appetite for entertainment content, it presents a big market opportunity, with analysts expecting the industry to cross $3-$4 billion in annual revenue by 2030. Last year, dedicated apps like Story TV, Kuku TV, and Quick TV were among the top downloaded video streaming apps in the country.
Founded in 2020 by former Flipkart exec Saurabh Pandey, the Story TV platform has taken off in the last few years with a catalog of over 5,000 titles in six languages. Pandey told TechCrunch that because of the snackable content format, users log 95 minutes on the app on average through multiple sessions in a day.
“I fundamentally believe that the next billion users will probably not grow up on a diet of watching television; they will grow up on a diet of watching content on their phones, right? And this content has to be, and this entertainment, designed very differently. It’s not going to be appointment viewing. It’s going to be within certain slots throughout the day. And a lot of this was earlier solved for short clips, but serialized storytelling was never solved,” Pandey said about the microdrama format.
He believes that there still will be a place for big-screen viewing with family or friends, but the majority of entertainment consumption would be done through mobile.
All microdrama platforms compete against platforms like YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok, where creators are posting content for free. Some of them are also creating a way for creators to post serialized content. Pandey thinks that producing quality content on the platform will entice users to choose StoryTV over other free platforms. The company points to its partnerships, such as the one with Indian TV production company Balaji Telefilms, to produce content.
The company offers different kinds of subscriptions ranging from monthly, quarterly, and yearly to unlock content. It also offers some free content supported by ads, which might not be as lucrative a medium to make money as subscriptions, according to reports.
Monetization is a challenge in India, as users often stick around for free content, but few convert to paid users. A report from analyst firm Redseer indicates that more than 40 million people have paid for microdrama at least once, but only 15-17 million users pay for it on a monthly basis. A separate survey by Ormax Media suggested that 72% of people haven’t ever paid while consuming microdrama.
AI and other bets
All microdrama platforms want to have enough supply to engage different audiences and want to involve AI to solve that. Some platforms, like Google-backed Kuku, want to improve workflows and create more content, and some platforms like Dashverse’s Shortfree want to use video AI models to create serialized clips.
At the moment, StoryTV falls into the first camp with its Dolphin AI platform. Started as an internal tool to improve video creation, the company is now planning to make the tool widely available. It can act as an editor with templates and an array of models to create images, audio, and video, according to its website.
EloElo’s vision is to have people use this tool for marketing campaigns and ads as well. Notably, while Indian platforms like Pocket and Kuku have built AI tools and given them to creators, it is likely to accelerate their content pipeline. But at InVideo, there hasn’t been a scaled effort to provide a good alternative to CapCut or Instagram Edits to creators from India.
Pandey believes that human involvement is still paramount to producing good stories, and AI tools are still creative directors for steering.
“My belief in involving AI is that AI is a really fast race car where AI is the engine, but you need an extremely capable Formula One driver to be on the steering wheel. That, for me, is the creative director or the showrunner. AI is supposed to work with them, augmenting their skill set. AI can help write stories, but so far the best stories I have loved have all had a very high human x AI element to it,” he said.
Besides microdrama, the company also has a vertical video learning app, Master, competing with the likes of Seekho and Kuku’s Guru, and an AI companion app, Voxy AI. The company said that it has more than 40 million monthly users across its apps. While it didn’t bifurcate users by app, the majority of users belong to Story TV.
EloElo currently has 240 people and wants to hire to increase the size of its AI and machine learning research team. The company is also deploying a good chunk of its capital to produce more original titles.
MIT Investment Co., along with existing investors like Play Ventures, Kalaari Capital, Waterbridge Ventures, and Griffin Gaming Partners, invested in the round.

articles.title: Apple’s latest watchOS beta includes its new always-on Audio Intelligence features
articles.body:
Starting today, Siri can tune into the Apple Watch’s mic with Audio Intelligence features that are available in the new watchOS 27.3 developer beta rolling out now. The two new additions are Siri Recap, which uses “ambient listening” to generate summaries of your conversation, and Live Rewind, which generates text transcripts of the last 15 seconds of audio your watch’s mic detected.
Apple’s latest watchOS beta includes its new always-on Audio Intelligence features
Audio Intelligence lets Siri ‘rewind’ and summarize audio from your Watch’s mic.
Apple is also releasing its redesigned Health app for testing today in the iOS 27.3 developer beta, and announced expanded language support in global English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), French, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Turkish, and Vietnamese. It adds sections like a new Insights tab with summaries for heart, sleep, fitness, and other data that pop up during the day, a For You section with personalized recommendations, and health content like educational videos and articles.
- Live Rewind, which can help users recall what was just said in conversation. A double-press of the Digital Crown shows the previous 15 seconds of a conversation as a text snippet, so the user can catch something they may have missed or are less familiar with. Users can ask Siri about the content of the text or save it to the Siri app to revisit later.
- Siri Recap, which can create high-level summaries of conversations that users can review later to jog their memory. When Siri Recap is turned on, after a conversation, Apple Intelligence automatically generates a title and key points in the new Siri app, allowing users to be more present and engaged in the moment.
When it comes to the implications of an ambient, always-listening AI, Apple has released this Audio Intelligence
Privacy Overview (pdf) about how it plans to protect users’ privacy when their watch is listening around the clock. It goes into detail about Apple’s claims that users’ raw audio “is handled within dedicated hardware, is not saved as a file, and is not accessible to the operating system, apps, or Apple.” According to Apple, “If you use iCloud with two-factor authentication and have a device passcode, any Siri Recap summary or Live Rewind text snippet you choose to save syncs across your devices end-to-end encrypted in the Siri app.”

articles.title: Tell HN: Gemini trains on chat history, even for subscribers (personal accounts)
articles.body:
If you have a personal Google AI subscription, all your saved chat history in Gemini can be used for training and there is no way to opt out unless you turn off chat history or use temporary chat sessions. These chat transcripts may even be read by human reviewers. Although Google claims to disconnect them from your account when human-reviewed, they explicitly warn 
not to enter confidential information
.
https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16836988
“[Gemini app activity] is used to improve Google services for everyone, including by training generative AI models, if your Keep Activity setting is on.“
https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961?hl=en#human_review
“A subset of chats are reviewed by human reviewers”
https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961?hl=en#pn_retain_data
“Chats reviewed by human reviewers [...] are not deleted when you delete your activity. Instead, they are retained for up to three years.”
https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961?hl=en#pn_data_usage
“Please don’t enter confidential information that you wouldn’t want a reviewer to see or Google to use to improve our services, including machine-learning technologies.”
To disable their training on your chat sessions, you need to turn off “Keep Activity” in Gemini’s settings. Turning that off means you’ll lose any chat sessions after 72 hours.
I learned this too late, thinking that having a paid subscription = not being turned into the product. Apparently paying is not enough.
Thank you to this user on HN for mentioning in another thread: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50355424

articles.title: Google’s Gemini-powered Home Speaker is already on sale for 20 percent off
articles.body:
If you’re looking for a good smart speaker, the Google Home Speaker is down to around $79 ($20 off) in all four colors at Best Buy, Walmart, and Target. That’s the best price we’ve seen for the Gemini-powered speaker, which launched in June and represents Google’s first smart speaker in several years.
Google’s Gemini-powered Home Speaker is already on sale for 20 percent off
Google’s latest smart speaker offers surprisingly good sound for its size, Gemini-powered voice controls, and more.
In her review, my colleague Jennifer Pattison Tuohy noted that Google’s new Home Speaker offers a nice balance of sound quality, size, and design. It’s smaller than the prior-gen Nest Audio, making it easy to place anywhere in your home. However, despite its small size, it produces loud, clear audio with 360-degree sound. Our own David Pierce even found it sounded cleaner, louder, and sharper than Amazon’s similarly priced Echo Dot Max, though Tuohy preferred the latter’s fuller sound and stronger bass. The older Nest Audio still sounds better overall, but Google’s latest speaker takes up less space and costs slightly less.
The Google Home Speaker also offers a few useful smart home upgrades. It supports Matter and includes a Thread border router, allowing you to connect and control a wide range of compatible smart home devices. It’s also the first Google smart speaker that can double as an audio output for the Google TV Streamer 4K, letting you play TV audio through one or two speakers instead of your TV’s built-in speakers. Tuohy found it worked well and delivered clear dialogue, though sound quality varied depending on what she was watching.
One of its most notable features is support for Gemini, which is also available on older Google speakers and is much better at understanding natural language and complex requests than the old Google Assistant. In her testing, Tuohy found it could handle multiple smart home commands at once and respond to conversational requests, like turning down the air conditioner when she mentioned feeling too hot. It’s also particularly impressive at answering general knowledge questions, though it can be slow and unreliable at times. Keep in mind, too, that some features require a $10-a-month Google Home Premium subscription, including Gemini Live, which lets you have extended conversations with the assistant without repeating the wake word.
